The tell for founders is that the AI buildout is now a leveraged bet on demand curves, with data-center moratoriums like New York's starting to price into where that capacity can actually go.

title: OpenAI wraps $7 billion share sale ahead of potential IPO
blurb: OpenAI completed a roughly $7 billion secondary share sale that lets current and former employees cash out at an $852 billion valuation, up from the $500 billion mark on its October tender. The sale relieves near-term liquidity pressure ahead of an IPO whose prospectus it filed confidentially in June. Tender offers are now a standard part of OpenAI's pre-IPO playbook, and Anthropic sits in the same position, meaning the two largest private AI companies are both managing employee liquidity while they decide when to test public markets.

title: Longtime OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap leaves as shake-up at AI lab continues
blurb: OpenAI COO turned "special projects" lead Brad Lightcap is leaving to start something new, the latest exit in a run of senior departures. He follows product and business chief Fidji Simo out the door last month and three other execs in April, thinning the bench as OpenAI tries to justify an $852B valuation and prep a monster IPO. This is the same operator who scaled the go-to-market team from around 50 people to more than 700 in 18 months, so the loss lands hardest on the revenue engine investors are pricing.

title: Wall Street just endorsed Jensen Huang's 'big concept' for AI. What now?
blurb: Nvidia's Jensen Huang lined up Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, Blackstone, KKR, Apollo, and Brookfield behind a plan to raise $500 billion or more for AI data-center construction, reframing AI infrastructure as a new asset class financed by Wall Street rather than tech balance sheets. The shift matters because the first three years of the build-out ran on record equity and debt, pushing some hyperscalers cash-flow negative, and McKinsey pegs total outlays at $7 trillion by decade's end. The announcement was thin on specifics, with signed memos of understanding but no contracts, interest rates, or named borrowers yet.

title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
blurb: Igor Babuschkin, a co-founder of xAI, left to start River, a company betting that AI should be open-source and trainable by anyone rather than locked inside a big lab. The pitch is that users own and shape the model for their own needs instead of renting behavior the vendor decides. It runs against the frontier labs' walled-garden playbook, and it's a signal that some of the people who built those closed systems now think the durable position is the one that hands control back to the customer.

title: Skan AI, which is building a "context graph of work" by observing staff using enterprise software, raised a $63M Series C co-led by Cathay Innovation and Dell (Michael Nuñez/VentureBeat)
blurb: Skan AI raised a $63M Series C co-led by Cathay Innovation and Dell to build what it calls a "context graph of work" by watching how staff actually use enterprise software. The pitch is that mapping real workflows from observed behavior gives AI agents the ground truth they need to automate steps that process-mining and documentation miss. For founders, it signals where enterprise automation money is moving: away from generic copilots and toward systems that learn the messy, undocumented way work actually gets done.

title: Kalshi brings in former U.S. solicitor general as Washington state gambling case escalates
blurb: Kalshi hired former U.S. Acting Solicitor General Neal Katyal as it fights Washington state over whether federal CFTC oversight preempts state gambling law, a question that will decide if prediction markets can operate nationwide regardless of local bans. A Seattle judge already rejected that preemption defense and granted an injunction, but Kalshi is still live in the state weeks later while its appeal proceeds and rival rulings pile up on both sides. The outcome sets the regulatory boundary for every prediction-market startup, not just Kalshi.

title: What’s Scaleup Europe, the $5.7B fund that just backed satellite company ICEYE?
blurb: The European Commission's Scaleup Europe Fund is now operational, and its first deal is co-leading the Series F of Finnish satellite-intelligence company ICEYE, valued above $11B. The vehicle plans to deploy €5B ($5.7B) into growth-stage EU startups in strategic sectors, but the structure is the real signal: it's backed by private investors and run by asset manager EQT rather than managed directly by Brussels. The bet is that Europe keeps losing deep-tech companies at the late stage because the growth capital sits abroad, and public money paired with a private manager is the attempt to close that gap.

title: Former Alibaba star researcher Junyang Lin launches Shanghai-based Pragmatik Labs to build digital and physical AI agents; Pragmatik hit a $2B valuation in June (Juro Osawa/The Information)
blurb: Junyang Lin, a lead researcher behind Alibaba's Qwen models, left to start Shanghai-based Pragmatik Labs, which is building both digital and physical AI agents and already hit a $2B valuation in June. The raise lands before any product ships, which is the going rate for a founder with frontier-lab credentials in China's agent race. The bet spanning software and robotics signals that the next wave of Chinese AI startups is chasing embodied agents, not another chat model, and the capital is following the pedigree rather than the traction.

title: Vacuum Pump Makers, Producers of Gases Are the New AI Winners
blurb: The AI trade is quietly moving down the supply chain to the companies that make the physical guts of chip production. European makers of vacuum pumps, heat exchangers, and specialty gases are emerging as under-owned winners of the AI boom, riding demand from the fabs building the chips everyone else fights over. For investors wary of stretched valuations on the obvious AI names, the pick-and-shovel suppliers offer exposure to the same buildout without paying frontier multiples.

title: Jumia Wins IFC, Axian Backing in $50 Million Equity Fundraising
blurb: Jumia raised $50M in fresh equity from its largest shareholder Axian and the World Bank's IFC, as the African e-commerce company pushes toward its first-ever profit. The IFC's involvement matters more than the size of the round, signaling that development-finance capital now sees a credible path to sustainable margins in African online retail. For a market long treated as a cash-burn experiment, the operator takeaway is that profitability, not just GMV growth, is becoming the bar African tech has to clear to keep raising.

title: African e-commerce company Jumia raised $50M, including $25M from the World Bank's IFC; Jumia's US-listed shares have fallen from $60+ in 2021 to $6 now (Loni Prinsloo/Bloomberg)
blurb: Jumia raised $50M, including $25M from the World Bank's IFC, a lifeline for African e-commerce built on patient development capital rather than the public markets. The company's US-listed shares have collapsed from above $60 in 2021 to around $6 today, a 90% drop that tracks the wider retreat from unprofitable growth stories. When public markets stop funding a category, the money that keeps it alive increasingly comes from development finance and strategic backers willing to underwrite the long build rather than the next quarter.

title: AI’s costly buildout complicates the Fed’s inflation fight
blurb: AI's promised deflation isn't showing up, and the buildout is doing the opposite in the near term. US capex on data centers and infrastructure is set to hit $581B this year, roughly 1.8% of GDP and climbing toward 2.8% by 2028, while only 17% to 20% of businesses report using AI and productivity gains stay invisible in the data. The costs land now, in higher electricity prices and snarled supply chains, before any payoff arrives, which leaves the Fed managing inflation the boom was supposed to cure.

title: CoreWeave surges 18% in premarket after a 'cleaner quarter.' Here's what's happening
blurb: CoreWeave's Q2 revenue doubled to $2.6B on hyperscaler demand for AI compute, and the stock jumped 18% premarket on what Citi called one of its cleaner quarters since going public. Yet operating expenses more than doubled and edged past revenue, leaving a $49M operating loss, so the scale story still runs ahead of profitability. The signal founders should read is in the backlog: $104B booked as of June 30, plus $25B in new third-quarter commitments and an extra $21B from Meta, which is why the market keeps funding the losses.

title: World's largest sovereign wealth fund posts record $184 billion profit as it reveals SpaceX stake for the first time
blurb: Norway's $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, posted a record half-year profit of $184.9 billion on a 9.4% return driven by a rally in Asian tech stocks. In the same report it disclosed a SpaceX stake for the first time, a 0.05% position worth $1.2 billion that makes it a major backer of both of Elon Musk's public and private ventures. The size signals where passive index-scale capital is now flowing: even the most diversified public investor on earth wants exposure to the marquee private names, and the biggest ones can now command a slice of a $2.3 trillion book.

title: Intel upsizes stock offering to $20 billion at $95 per share as AI demand accelerates
blurb: Intel upsized its common stock offering to $20B at $95 per share, raising net proceeds of about $19.7B to fund capital expenditures and factory tooling as AI demand accelerates. The raise comes off a run where the stock surged 175% in 2026 and quintupled over the last year, backed partly by the government's 10% equity stake. The signal for founders is that even a legacy chipmaker now has to fund the AI build-out at hyperscaler scale, with industry capex on track to hit $765B this year and $1.2T in 2027.

title: SpaceXAI's Grok Bot turns agents into persistent digital coworkers that can operate your apps for $120-per-month
blurb: SpaceXAI, the SpaceX division formerly known as xAI, launched a beta of Grok Bot, persistent agents that sign into your apps, work while your laptop is closed, and return with finished deliverables or an approval request. Pricing starts at $120 per seat per month for teams and $200 per month for individuals. It arrives into a crowded field alongside Anthropic's Claude Cowork and OpenAI's Workspace Agents, and SpaceXAI shipped no benchmarks to separate it from them.

title: TripleDart tops $7 million ARR with AI-led growth, reports 50 per cent EBIT margin
blurb: TripleDart, a bootstrapped Bengaluru B2B marketing company, crossed $7M in ARR at a 50% EBIT margin, and says software rather than headcount or capital drove the jump. That lands in the middle of the services-as-software bet, where investors have poured more than $300M this year into startups trying to run labor-heavy services at software margins, most of them proving it on a single slice like SEO or content. TripleDart claims it did it across the entire inbound marketing function with no funding, running client work through an in-house agent platform called Slate.

title: Peter Steinberger on building in the agent era
blurb: Peter Steinberger spent 13 years building PSPDFKit, sold it, swore off founding again, then agents got good enough to pull him back as the creator of OpenClaw. His lesson is that the job has shifted from writing code to engineering the pipeline that lets an agent write, review, and test it end to end. He credits his edge to having run a company before, which taught him to design the loop rather than just prompt for output.

title: Some Simple Economics of Open versus Closed AI
blurb: The open-versus-closed AI fight is arguing over the wrong margin, according to a new a16z piece drawing on economist Petra Moser's study of 15,000 inventions from the 1851 and 1876 world's fairs. That data found patent protection had no effect on how much innovation happened, only on where it was directed. Applied to AI, open weights likely won't change the overall level of investment, only its direction: what gets built, who builds it, and who captures the returns. Closed labs keep pushing the general frontier while open weights spread experimentation across firms and domains.

title: Can software factories actually work?
blurb: Software factories automate the coding pipeline so agents can pull tickets, ship PRs, and deploy through CI/CD while humans read less and less of the output. The debate is whether the "lights-off" version, where agents write everything and humans review nothing, can hold up at scale, and HumanLayer's Dex Horthy argues no harness ever makes it work. Most teams sit in the middle: PostHog's agents write about 70% of PRs, but humans still skim 80% of them.

title: Nvidia turns compute into collateral; Intel prices $20 billion at a discount
blurb: Nvidia signed preliminary deals with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to raise more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure, using the compute itself as collateral. Special-purpose entities would issue debt, buy Nvidia systems, and lease them to customers who add capacity without touching their own balance sheets, while Nvidia backstops up to 25% of residual value, a ceiling near $125 billion. The catch is that Nvidia's obligation grows exactly when used systems lose value, the same condition that would weaken demand for new ones.

title: UK cybersecurity startup Cytix raises €6 million Series A to tackle AI-driven software change risks
blurb: Cytix raised €6M ($7M) in a Series A led by Northern Gritstone to sell a platform that governs the security risk created by AI-assisted software change. The bet is that agentic workflows and continuous delivery now ship code at machine speed, outpacing security models built for human-paced releases and leaving few security leaders with real control over what changed. Cytix reaches enterprise and regulated buyers, where change governance is a compliance obligation, directly and through managed-service deals with NCC Group and KPMG.

title: Edgify raises $9M to expand its edge AI platform
blurb: Edgify raised $9M in a Series A+ from Rank Ventures and Mangrove Capital Partners, bringing total funding to $25M for its edge AI platform that turns self-checkouts, cameras, scales, and point-of-sale systems into a coordinated intelligence layer. Devices process and learn locally instead of shipping raw data to the cloud, cutting latency and infrastructure cost while keeping customer data in the store. The company started in grocery loss prevention and is now moving into convenience stores, quick-service restaurants, and distribution centers, betting the same legacy-hardware problem repeats across every industry where fleets of devices meet the physical world.

title: Ex-Meta AI research director raises $10.25M from Trilogy and Madrona for stealth physical AI startup
blurb: Ex-Meta AI research director Kevin Carlberg raised $10.25M from Trilogy and Madrona for Noosphere Labs, a stealth physical-AI startup.

title: Again acquires Geno to combine AI-driven discovery with industrial biomanufacturing
blurb: Again acquired Genomatica (Geno) to build a biomanufacturing platform that spans AI-driven molecule discovery through industrial-scale production, with terms undisclosed. The prize is Geno's computational biotech platform, patent portfolio, and data across experimental research and scale-up, which Again will fold into its own modeling to shorten development cycles for new production pathways. The bet is that AI molecule design only pays off if it survives the jump to commercial-scale execution, so the combined company will license its tech, co-develop pathways with industrial partners, and manufacture products directly.

title: HSBC Asset Management invests in London-founded Model ML
blurb: HSBC Asset Management has taken an equity stake in Model ML, the London-founded startup automating research, due diligence, and document workflows for banks and asset managers, pushing its total raised past $100M. The signal is a bank's own money backing vertical AI for financial services, with Deloitte and PwC already on the client list a year after the $75M Series A. Model ML's bet is orchestration over any single model, routing each task to whichever model fits, and a strategic buyer that becomes a customer is worth more than the check.

title: Stockholm’s Quartr lands €15.6 million to expand its AI-ready public company IR data coverage
blurb: Quartr raised €15.6M led by Altos to expand IR data coverage across 15,000+ companies, with ~120% net revenue retention.

title: European space-tech funding reached €2.9 billion in H1 2026, up 622%, but debt and a handful of sovereign-infrastructure bets explain most of the apparent explosion
blurb: European space-tech funding hit €2.9 billion in H1 2026, up 622% on last year, but the headline hides how the money actually moved. Almost half of it was debt, and the ten largest rounds absorbed 91.5% of all disclosed capital, led by nearly €1 billion of export-credit financing for Eutelsat's OneWeb satellites and €900 million across three ICEYE entries. The real signal isn't a venture boom but sovereign infrastructure and industrial policy, with governments funding Earth-observation and satellite capacity they increasingly treat as strategic rather than speculative.

title: Europe’s AI watermarking rules are now live, but visible labels, hidden machine-readable marks and editorial review apply to different companies, content and moments under Article 50
blurb: Europe's AI transparency rules under Article 50 of the AI Act have been enforceable since August 2, but "AI watermarking" hugely undersells what the law actually demands. The obligations split by role: system providers must build machine-readable, provenance-style marks into synthetic text, audio, images, and video, while deployers like publishers and freelancers owe a separate human-facing disclosure in narrower cases such as deepfakes and unreviewed public-interest text. If you develop or operate an AI system touching the EU market, compliance now turns on who controls the system, how content was made, and why it was published.

title: HSBC Asset Management backs AI finance group Model ML
blurb: HSBC Asset Management invested in Model ML, a 2023 fintech building an agentic operating system for financial services, through the VC strategy inside its $81B alternatives platform. The bet isn't on a single model but on the orchestration layer, a model-agnostic engine that routes financial research, due diligence, modeling, and document generation to the best underlying model while enforcing enterprise governance and auditability. A frontier lab's incumbent customer backing vertical AI signals where the value is landing: not the model, but the software that governs and coordinates many of them inside a regulated workflow.

title: Flying-taxi maker Vertical Aerospaces secures £74m
blurb: Vertical Aerospace raised $100M (£74m) to push its Valo eVTOL toward certification and commercialization. The round pairs $40m from Mudrick Capital, $35m in fresh equity, and a $25m preferred-equity issuance, buying the Bristol company more runway after piloted transition demos at Farnborough. The cash triples battery production capacity and funds a hybrid-electric prototype retrofit for flight testing in early 2027, a sign that even the most capital-hungry eVTOL bets are still finding money to close the gap between demo flights and a commercial aircraft.

title: Why deeptech founders are dictating term sheets in 2026 — and how you can secure a fair deal
blurb: UK venture has split into a barbell, and deeptech and AI founders are on the winning end, commanding founder-friendly terms while every other sector gets squeezed. Larger deals now make up 31% of all term sheets, up from 26% in 2024, as investors pile capital into fewer high-growth companies. The leverage is real but conditional: it only shows up once you have more than one term sheet, so the move is to manufacture competition among investors and use it to hold board control and cut the day-to-day decisions that need their sign-off.

title: UK air defence startup Cambridge Aerospace hits $3.4bn valuation in new fundraise
blurb: Cambridge Aerospace raised $300M at a $3.4bn valuation, led by DFJ Growth, just months after a $200M Series B. The two-year-old British startup makes Skyhammer, a drone and low-speed missile interceptor already under contract with the UK armed forces and tested in Jordan. Defense capital is flowing to air defense specifically because modern conflicts in Ukraine and Iran exposed the gap, and investors want systems that are faster to build and cheaper to field, which is pulling frontier venture money into hardware that ships to governments rather than software that ships to enterprises.

title: Tony Blair’s son seeks $200m for new defence startup, reports say
blurb: Nick Blair, son of former UK prime minister Tony Blair, is reportedly seeking around $200m for Pyra, a London defence startup building software to integrate disparate defence systems into a single source. The raise lands amid a surge of capital into European defence tech, where startups pulled in €2.3bn last year, more than double the 2024 total, as governments boost military spending and push for sovereign capability. It is Blair's second defence venture after Skyral, the simulation startup he chairs, which raised $20m last year.

title: Ex-LocalGlobe trio plots new VC firm
blurb: Three investors who left Phoenix Court, the firm behind seed fund LocalGlobe, are in early talks to raise their own fund. Catherine Lenson, Mish Mashkautsan and George Henry all exited earlier this year, and their move continues a pattern of senior partners spinning out of established European firms to run smaller, founder-led vehicles. The pitch will hinge on whether their LocalGlobe track record translates into LP commitments in a market where new managers are struggling to close first-time funds.

title: Accel raises $800m for ninth early-stage Europe fund
blurb: Accel raised $800m for its ninth Europe and Israel early-stage fund, plus another $2.7bn across three other funds, just two years after its last $650m European vehicle. The firm has backed almost 250 European companies over 25 years, from UiPath to Monzo to Doctolib, and is now steering capital toward the region's two hottest themes: defence and AI, with recent bets on Lovable, n8n, Cambridge Aerospace, and Legora. For founders, it signals that US multi-stage capital is committing harder to European companies building for global markets from day one.

title: Exclusive: ClearJet raises $25M to build the ‘Uber of Cargo’
blurb: ClearJet raised a $25M Series B led by Edison Partners to scale an asset-light "Uber for cargo" model that moves e-commerce packages on unused capacity aboard passenger flights already flying between U.S. cities. The pitch is cheaper and faster logistics without owning a fleet, cutting shipping costs by up to 35% and shaving one to three days off delivery across a network spanning 95 airports. The model is already working: the Austin startup is profitable, tripled revenue year over year, and moves 30M packages annually, still a sliver of the 1.8B U.S. parcels it considers air-eligible.

title: The VC Firm That Helped Build Latin America’s Startup Scene Is Crossing Into Silicon Valley
blurb: Monashees, Latin America's oldest major VC firm, opened a permanent San Francisco office in September 2025 to wire its portfolio into Bay Area capital and AI research. The bet is that LatAm's next phase runs through Silicon Valley, and the firm is already co-investing with Google through the Gama Fund, which backs Brazilian AI-native startups at up to $2M per deal. Brazil is the proof point, with a payments rail in Pix used by more than 90% of adults and ChatGPT's third-largest market by visitor share.

title: From Kraken to KuCoin: Entravel raises $7.5M for its push beyond crypto
blurb: Entravel raised $7.5M, co-led by Ethereal Ventures and Finality Capital, to take its crypto-exchange travel booking tech mainstream.

title: Skan AI raises $63 million betting that watching how employees actually work is the missing layer of enterprise AI
blurb: Skan AI raised $63M in a Series C co-led by Cathay Innovation and Dell Technologies Capital, betting that the missing layer of enterprise AI is watching how employees actually work rather than reading how they're supposed to. The pitch lands against a brutal backdrop: Gartner finds only 8% of enterprises have AI agents in production, and 95% of early implementations will need a full redesign. The argument is that models aren't the problem, the map is, and the gap between documented process and real work is exactly where agents fail.

title: Manus will return to operating as an independent company
blurb: Manus is splitting back into an independent company and, to satisfy regulators in certain jurisdictions, will delete data generated by some users after December 29, 2025, with a backup window closing August 23. The move reads as another cross-border AI startup unwinding its structure to stay legal in multiple markets at once. For founders serving users globally, it is a reminder that data residency and jurisdictional rules can force a product to wipe accounts on a fixed calendar, no matter how much goodwill the company has built.

title: AI insurance startup Axle raises $17.5M from Base10 Partners to automate policy workflows
blurb: Axle raised a $17.5M Series A led by Base10 Partners, roughly four times its total prior funding, to build an AI-native clearinghouse for insurance. The pitch is that credit, payments, identity, and income all run through a clearinghouse in the middle, and insurance never got one, so a mortgage lender still calls a carrier ten-plus times a year to confirm a single policy is active. Axle already clears more than $100B in coverage annually across 4,000-plus customers including Rocket Mortgage and Experian, and the bet is that standardized, programmable insurance becomes the layer everyone else builds on.

title: The cost floor under the physical AI boom
blurb: Money is flowing back into robots, and the whole physical-AI data layer rests on one claim almost nobody outside these companies checks: that you can ingest, process, and verify petabytes of first-person video cheaply enough to sell it at a margin. Mecka AI raised $60M on exactly that bet, and firms like Scale AI, Wayve, and MicroAGI are chasing the same picks-and-shovels position for robotics that labeling built for language models. The moment the cost curve stops being linear, which at petabyte scale arrives sooner than anyone budgets for, the margin under the entire boom moves.

title: Danish Entravel Group raises €6.5 million to secure larger supplier credit facilities
blurb: Danish TravelTech Entravel Group raised €6.5M to expand supplier credit, scale bookings, and push its white-label travel stack into new platforms.

title: Infrastructure and compute: Enterprises are buying AI compute for speed while flying blind on what it costs
blurb: Enterprise AI has crossed into production, with two-thirds of 170 enterprises now running workloads live and three in 10 at scale, but the ability to account for what that compute costs hasn't kept up. Under production pressure, teams have quietly demoted total cost of ownership below performance and GPU availability, and rank reliability above price as the measure of success. The bill is the blind spot: fewer than half rigorously track what their AI compute costs, and 69% of enterprises running their own GPUs report utilization at 50% or less.

title: Sector Snapshot: Fitness Startup Funding Is Rebounding, But Investors Want AI And Data, Not Treadmills
blurb: Fitness and wellness startups pulled in more than $3.6B in the first half of 2026, on pace to run about a third ahead of 2025 and top every year since 2022. But the money is concentrating into fewer, larger bets on devices that collect health data continuously and use AI to turn it into personalized guidance, not the connected-hardware plays of the pandemic era. Whoop raised a $575M Series G, while Tonal and Hydrow, the treadmill-and-mirror generation, haven't seen new investment in three-plus years.

title: Mojo 1.0
blurb: Modular released Mojo 1.0, marking the language stable and production-ready after building toward the milestone since its 2023 debut. The 26.5 release converges on single ways to express common patterns, with variables now always declared with var, unified closures, and a single Pointer type, and commits to primarily additive changes during the 1.x line while managing breaking changes like mature languages such as C++.

title: Over 2,500 Organizations Impacted by LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack
blurb: A supply chain attack on the LiteLLM Python library exposed an estimated 434,000 CI/CD pipelines and over 2,500 organizations, including Nvidia, AWS, and the London Stock Exchange Group, after two malicious versions reached PyPI. LiteLLM was compromised indirectly when its CI pipeline auto-installed a poisoned Trivy build, and although the tainted packages were live for only 40 minutes, the payload ran on every Python invocation and leaked cloud keys, SSH keys, and tokens.

title: H3-metal – Native MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple Silicon
blurb: h3.c is a native C implementation of MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple Silicon, running prompt-to-video and prompt-to-audio generation end to end through hand-written Metal blocks. It supports first/last-frame conditioning and ordered Ref2VA image references, plus an Iris-style interactive session that keeps BF16 prompt conditioning and the video decoder in memory so re-seeding a prompt skips reloading and re-encoding.

title: Open-sourcing Metals v2: Databricks’ Java and Scala language server for multi‑million line codebases
blurb: Databricks open-sourced Metals v2, an extension of the Scala language server with first-class Java support and scaling for its 26M-line Bazel monorepo. Available now in Cursor, VS Code, and Neovim, it lets teams pair a coding agent with a lightweight editor instead of IntelliJ, which Databricks credits for pushing weekly active Cursor usage to 92% while it dropped most of its IntelliJ seats.

title: What I learned by putting GitHub Copilot behind a MitM proxy
blurb: Rafael routed GitHub Copilot's traffic through a MitM proxy to observe what VS Code actually sends at runtime, rather than reading through millions of lines of source. The post inspects Copilot's network calls, agent harness, and memory handling, arguing that the context assembled and shipped to the model, not the model itself, is becoming the real product.

title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Benchmarking Agents on Large-Scale Multilingual Code Refactoring
blurb: SWE-Bench ProMax is an expert-curated, multilingual refactoring benchmark of 170 real-commit instances across seven languages, averaging 11.4 modified files and 261.6 changed lines per task. The authors rewrote every issue spec from scratch and manually pruned overly narrow and overly broad tests to fix problems flagged in prior benchmarks, and the best frontier model resolves only 41.2% of tasks.

title: Docker Sandboxes – Disposable, isolated sandboxes for AI agents
blurb: Docker released Sandboxes, a CLI tool (`brew install docker/tap/sbx`) that runs AI coding agents inside disposable microVMs with user-defined network and filesystem controls. The microVM boundary makes YOLO mode (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) safe to run unattended, works with Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Codex, Kiro, and OpenCode, and lets agents spin up their own Docker containers without Docker Desktop.

title: AI code-testing startup Blacksmith’s valuation jumps almost 10x in less than a year
blurb: Blacksmith raised a $45M Series B led by Peak XV Partners at a $550M valuation, up from $60M when it raised its Series A less than a year ago. The startup runs CI workloads and ships Codesmith, an agent that auto-fixes failed code checks, and now serves 5,000+ customers including Supabase and Clerk in a market crowded by GitHub Actions and the cloud providers.

title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
blurb: Two malicious LiteLLM releases sat on PyPI for about 40 minutes on March 24, carrying code that harvested cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords from any system that installed versions 1.82.7 or 1.82.8. CloudSEK has now published a searchable dataset mapping potential exposure to over 2,500 organizations, including NVIDIA, Cisco, and FedEx, and both it and the FBI advise rotating any secrets accessible that day.

title: SpecPath: Testing Coding Agents Across Contract-Equivalent Specification Histories
blurb: SpecPath is a diagnostic that tests whether coding agents produce the same behavior when a requirement is reached through different but contract-equivalent revision histories, holding the repository, final spec, verifier, agent, and budget fixed while varying only the path. Across five tasks and 14 agent configurations, aggregate accuracy barely moved, yet 35 of 100 blocks that passed on the direct spec failed on at least one equivalent history.

title: Rust SIMD on the GPU
blurb: VectorWare got Rust's portable SIMD (core::simd) running on the GPU, mapping a `Simd<T, N>` vector directly onto a warp's 32 lanes since NVIDIA's SIMT model is SIMD with per-lane addressing. Because portable SIMD lives in core rather than std, developers can write architecture-agnostic vector arithmetic, reductions, and lane shuffles once and have the compiler lower them to GPU hardware, adding parallelism below the thread level the company's earlier warp-mapped threads left unused.

title: One Recipe, Many Harnesses: What Self-Evolution Encodes Across Languages and Models
blurb: This paper studies self-evolving harnesses for coding agents, holding one evolution recipe fixed across eight programming languages and three base models to analyze what the evolved artifacts actually encode. The authors find that harnesses share an abstract playbook across languages but implement it with mostly disjoint ecosystem tooling, and that the shared core distills into one universal harness while a language-specific margin resists transfer and needs native re-evolution.

title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding
blurb: This paper argues that agentic coding instruction files like CLAUDE.md grow without bound because appending is cheap while safely deleting an instruction whose rationale is gone costs exponential verification, a failure mode the authors call catastrophic remembering. Across 247,694 instruction lifetimes in 1,867 repos, prompts more than tripled over their lifetime and old instructions grew steadily harder to remove, with the proposed fix being prompt comments that encode latent reasoning.

title: Apple Silicon and macOS VMs: Faster LLM Inference with llama.cpp
blurb: Cua built a process-scoped compatibility layer that rewrites selected Metal capability answers for one guest process, letting llama.cpp pick newer GPU kernels inside a macOS VM running on Apple's Virtualization.framework. On an M1 Ultra the unlocked VM ran TinyLlama 1.1B prompt processing 11.08x faster and token generation 16.36x faster than the stock guest, reaching 98% to 99% of bare-metal speed, with build scripts and raw benchmark logs included for reproduction.

title: OpenSSH 10.5/10.5p1
blurb: OpenSSH 10.5 patches an ssh-agent flaw where a locked agent still honored session-bind@openssh.com requests, letting operations meant to stay local, including adding PKCS#11 tokens and using destination-restricted keys, run from a remote forwarded agent. The team also cited a rise in AI-assisted security reports and independent rediscovery of the same bugs, and will now ship more frequent releases rather than batching fixes.

title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Delivers Fast, Accurate Specialized Task Execution for Long-Running Agents
blurb: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters built for the high-volume execution layer of long-running agents. It ships with speculative decoding and harness-optimized training for tools like OpenClaw, alongside NeMo Switchyard, a routing library that sends each task to the cheapest model that can handle it.

title: Show HN: Woxi - Open-source Mathematica / Wolfram Language reimplementation
blurb: Woxi is an open-source reimplementation of the Wolfram Language and Mathematica that ships as a Jupyter kernel. Install it locally with `woxi install-kernel`, or run notebooks in the browser through the bundled JupyterLite instance with no local setup required.

title: GitSkills: A Dataset of Agent Skills on GitHub
blurb: GitSkills is a dataset of 3,797,117 SKILL.md files collected from 282,200 public GitHub repositories in July 2026, capturing how developers write, reuse, and maintain the agent-skill format Anthropic introduced in October 2025. The authors deduplicate to 1,877,981 distinct contents, enrich one representative per group with parsed front matter, folder contents, repo metadata, and partial commit history, and ship it as a single SQLite file for research on adoption, reuse, authorship, maintenance, and security.

title: TDD inside the agent loop - theater or actual value?
blurb: Martin Fowler's team ran an exploratory eval on whether forcing a coding agent to follow TDD fully inside its own loop actually improves output, generating small, medium, and large greenfield tasks with Sonnet 4.6 and grading them with Opus. The result was no discernible quality gain, with non-TDD solutions occasionally ranked slightly higher on design and test quality and no meaningful difference in mutation scores.

title: Go is an ideal language for AI-assisted software engineering
blurb: Google argues that as AI generates most code, a language's value shifts from how fast it lets you write to how easily humans can review, verify, and maintain what the agent produced. The post makes the case that Go's opinionated simplicity, uniform formatting and tooling, and long-term compatibility guarantees make agent-written code cheaper to read and safer to keep in production over years.

title: Build Low-Latency Multilingual Voice Agents: Open Weights & Full Deployment Control with NVIDIA Magpie TTS
blurb: NVIDIA released Magpie Multilingual TTS, an open-weights text-to-speech model with production NVIDIA NIM packaging and support for 12 languages, now adding Modern Standard Arabic, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese. The open weights let teams run TTS as a tunable component in a cascaded ASR/LLM/TTS pipeline on their own infrastructure, trading the simplicity of a single integrated speech API for control over latency, data residency, and domain-specific voice customization.

title: Agentic Code Quality
blurb: Addy Osmani argues that code review no longer scales as the primary quality check once agents generate hundreds of thousands of changes a day, so quality now depends on the constraints you wrap around them. He frames quality gates such as unit and property tests, mutation testing, and complexity metrics as the deterministic loop that decides whether an agent's proposal is safe, correct, and scoped enough to ship.

title: Illinois just passed a law that puts Linux on the hook for age verification
blurb: Illinois signed HB5511 (Public Act 104-0664) on July 31, which defines an "operating system provider" broadly enough to cover anyone shipping an internet-connected OS and requires them to build an age-declaration step and hand an age-bracket signal to any app that asks by January 1, 2028. Unlike Colorado, Illinois added no open source exemption, so hobbyist and nonprofit OS projects fall under the same mandate as commercial vendors.

title: Message your other Claude Code sessions
blurb: Claude Code v2.1.224 adds cross-session messaging, letting one session hand a finding, status, or decision to another through the new ListAgents and SendMessage tools without you copy-pasting between terminals. It works on macOS and Linux with no setup once sessions meet the version requirement, covers parallel worktrees and long-running jobs, and can reply to sessions on other machines though cross-machine exchanges must be started locally.

title: Security Tests as Executable Specifications for LLM Code Generation: Benefits, Trade-offs, and Coverage Limits
blurb: This paper tests security tests as executable specifications for LLM code generation, using a scaffold called SecTDD across 2,705 trajectories, 16 CWE categories, and two model families. Showing all visible tests upfront lifts hidden functional-and-security joint success by 19.3 points on average but helps only seven of nine benchmark-model conditions, and candidates that pass every visible test still fail hidden behavior families.

title: Using the GitHub Copilot SDK for Java
blurb: GitHub released the Copilot SDK for Java, a client library that lets server-side Java code create Copilot agent sessions, register tools, send prompts, and receive structured responses using CompletableFuture, annotations, lambdas, and virtual threads. Unlike Langchain4j or Spring AI, it carries no framework dependency and its BYOK support keeps it AI-vendor neutral, running in Jakarta EE and Spring environments via a Maven dependency currently at 1.0.7-preview.1.

title: Understanding the Architecture of Coding Agents: An Exploratory Study Using a Research Prototype
blurb: This paper documents the internal architecture of coding agents and introduces Ark, a minimal open-source agent that preserves the essential components while stripping everything else for teaching and research. Running gpt-5.4-mini, Ark solved 8 of 10 tasks on the accompanying ArkBench suite with modest token consumption, and the authors compare its design against state-of-the-art agents using a recent architectural taxonomy.

title: We Deleted Two Skills That Tried to Help
blurb: The team deleted two agent skills after a Forge release postmortem showed both quietly expanded a bounded "ship one change" task past any stable boundary. JFDI turned an operator's "approve everything" prompt into open-ended production authority with no stop condition, pushing main and applying migrations through cascading platform defects, while Maintainability Guardrails expanded what ordinary coding work appeared to require by attaching broad hardening obligations.

title: How and Why Netflix Built a Real-Time Distributed Graph: Part 3 — Querying the graph with gRPC execution API
blurb: The third installment of Netflix's distributed graph series details the gRPC-based execution API that serves queries against the graph, covering how the engine plans traversals, batches subqueries, and streams results back to callers. The design favors a typed gRPC contract over GraphQL at the storage layer, trading schema flexibility for tighter control over execution cost and predictable latency under Netflix's real-time read load.

title: Linus Torvalds says AI has made 'huge' Linux kernel updates the new normal
blurb: Linus Torvalds says AI-assisted contributions have pushed the Linux kernel to consistently large release cycles, with big updates now the baseline rather than the exception. He noted the shift raises the maintainer review burden, since human reviewers still have to vet code that AI tools can generate far faster than it can be checked.

title: Modular's Mojo programming language hits 1.0 milestone
blurb: Modular released version 1.0 of Mojo, its Python-superset language aimed at high-performance AI and systems code, marking the first stable release after years of preview. Developers are still waiting on the promised open source compiler to clear up uncertainty following Qualcomm's acquisition of Modular, which leaves the language's long-term governance and portability an open question.

title: Anthropic makes Claude Code’s auto mode default for paid users
blurb: Anthropic is making Claude Code's auto mode the default for Pro, Max, and Team plans starting August 14, letting the agent run tool calls without per-action approval while a classifier blocks irreversible or destructive commands and falls back to manual approval after three consecutive blocks. In Anthropic's testing the classifier caught 89% of deliberately dangerous commands versus 13.6% for human reviewers, with analysts flagging added latency, oversight, and security tradeoffs.

title: Show HN: Ante, a coding agent in a single binary that runs offline
blurb: Antigma Labs released Ante, a self-contained coding agent that ships as one ~15MB Rust binary with zero runtime dependencies and runs models locally via a pinned llama.cpp. It works like Claude Code or Codex without their model constraints, scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with open-weight DeepSeek V4 Flash, and uses roughly 7x less peak memory and 9x less average CPU than Claude Code across 20 parallel Docker tasks.

title: The best new features in Python 3.15
blurb: Python 3.15 reached its first release candidate with lazy imports that defer a module's cost until its code actually runs, plus new frozendict and sentinel() built-ins, better error messages, and faster JIT compilation. It also adds profiling.sampling, a statistical sampling profiler that trades cProfile's per-call precision for far lower runtime overhead, with the old deterministic profiler renamed to profiling.tracing.

title: Microsoft releases MAI-Code-1.1-Flash coding model to better compete with Chinese models
blurb: Microsoft released MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, a coding model that replaces MAI-Code-1-Flash and improves on it across development tasks, including a 22% gain on Terminal-Bench 2.1. The release positions Microsoft's in-house coding models against faster-moving Chinese open-weight competitors.

title: Cursor prepares to launch Origin platform for code reviews
blurb: Cursor is preparing to open Origin, its Graphite-built code review platform, beyond the closed partner beta, with interface strings pointing to a "Cursor Review" rollout as early as this week. The system adds an automated pull request pipeline that pings developers only when their judgment is needed, targeting the review bottleneck that stalls teams running fleets of background agents rather than the generation step.

title: AI code-testing startup Blacksmith raised a $45M Series B led by Peak XV Partners at a $550M valuation, up from $60M after it raised a $10M Series A in 2025 (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
blurb: Blacksmith, an AI code-testing startup, raised a $45M Series B led by Peak XV Partners at a $550M valuation, up nearly 10x from the $60M valuation it held after its $10M Series A in 2025. The round signals continued investor appetite for tooling that speeds CI and automated testing, a workflow layer developers increasingly expect to be AI-assisted.

title: Can software factories actually work?
blurb: PostHog examines whether "software factories" — pipelines where agents pull tickets, build PRs, and ship via CI/CD with minimal human review — can scale, weighing HumanLayer CEO Dex Horthy's viral argument that they never will against real-world adoption at Ramp, Cursor, Uber, and PostHog itself. The post frames autonomy as a spectrum, noting PostHog's agents write roughly 70% of its PRs while humans still skim at least 80% of them.

title: Comprendia: AI-Augmented Code Comprehension
blurb: Comprendia is an Eclipse plugin for Java that puts structural dependency visualization and LLM code explanation on one interactive graph, with overlays for clone detection and CVE risk. Its Graph-Aware Callee Pruning selects relevant callees using graph distance, inheritance collapse, and edge-type weighting, producing prompts that are reproducible across LLM families and traceable back to visible graph nodes.

title: CSS properties you should know for better text designs
blurb: Five CSS properties for standout web typography, including background-clip: text for image-filled letterforms and align-content for true vertical centering.

title: SmellCC: A Tool for Automated Code Smells Remediation
blurb: SmellCC is a VS Code extension that pairs SonarQube detection with an LLM pipeline to automatically refactor the ten most common Python code smells with one-click, in-place fixes. Using chain-of-thought prompting and few-shot examples, the tool reports a 96.8% cleaning rate at 91.3% accuracy while keeping the refactored code syntactically correct and behavior-preserving.

title: Why you might want to build your WebApp in Canvas instead of HTML
blurb: The author explains why performance-critical web apps like Google Docs, Miro, and Canva render their core surfaces on Canvas rather than the DOM, trading the browser's built-in layout, event handling, and reflow for a bare drawing API. Canvas skips HTML parsing, style computation, and reflow to gain speed and full rendering control for infinite workspaces and zoomable grids, at the cost of reimplementing text, accessibility, and hit-testing yourself.

title: Relying on Go
blurb: Solod is a systems language for C and Go developers that is literally a subset of Go, reusing its syntax highlighting, LSP, linters, package management, and much of its standard library code verbatim rather than trying to fix Go's mistakes. The trade-off is that Go's tooling doesn't know Solod is a subset, so it won't flag full-Go features that Solod doesn't support, and the language adds manual memory management with explicit allocators.

title: Vertical slices, their ownership and external dependencies
blurb: The author argues that vertical slices, modules, and bounded contexts get conflated, and that treating every application area as a fully autonomous bounded context sets the separation bar so high that any dependency between slices looks like a violation. The fix is defining what a slice does when it needs something external, since "minimise coupling" means non-zero, not the myth that slices can never share code or read what another slice wrote.

title: From Finding to Fixing: Reducing maintainer burden with automated patches
blurb: Google connected OSS-Fuzz to CodeMender, DeepMind's code-security agent, so that a fuzzer crash now feeds directly into an automated pipeline that finds the root cause and produces a validated patch. The system leans on fuzzing's near-zero false-positive rate to avoid the noise of agentic scanners, then has CodeMender explore code paths in parallel and validate that each patch preserves existing functionality before delivering it to maintainers.

title: Firma digital CAdES vs XAdES en Java: las diferencias que importan cuando tu CA te pide una y vos tenés la otra
blurb: CAdES vs XAdES in Java: why a cryptographically valid signature still fails validation when your CA expects the other format.

title: Show HN: Git-knife – Edit commit messages, authors, and dates like a spreadsheet
blurb: git-knife is a desktop GUI for editing git commit metadata directly, including message, author name/email, and the author and committer dates that GUIs like GitKraken, Fork, and Sublime Merge treat as immutable. It shells out to the system git CLI and rebuilds commits with git commit-tree, reusing each commit's original tree so file contents never change, and supports bulk regex edits with an automatic backup ref before every rewrite.

title: How Cursor Router chooses the right model for the task
blurb: Cursor Router picks a model per turn using Compass, a learned complexity predictor, plus a task taxonomy trained on live developer traffic rather than benchmark scores. Its Auto Intelligence mode now delivers above Fable-level user satisfaction at 68% lower cost, while Auto Balance outperforms Opus 4.8 at 41% lower cost with a slight satisfaction gain.

title: Metabase SQL Zero-Day Attacks Could Have Wide Blast Radius
blurb: Metabase disclosed a maximum-severity SQL-injection zero-day (CVSS 10, still no CVE) that let attackers gain remote admin access to instances, alter configuration, and steal credentials for every connected database. Metabase Cloud customers were auto-patched, but self-hosted deployments running version 1.58 or later with the /api/session/reset_password endpoint exposed to the internet remain exploitable and should lock that endpoint down immediately.

title: How We Pushed CDC into Postgres
blurb: Snowflake engineers detailed how they rebuilt Postgres change data capture from the ground up for Snowflake Postgres, replacing the usual pull-based logical decoding pipeline with a push model. The new data mirroring feature, now in public preview, pushes committed changes directly from Postgres into Apache Iceberg tables in transactional batches, then applies them to Snowflake serverlessly with low lag and transactional consistency. The pitch is one button instead of the fragile, high-cost replication tooling most teams stitch together themselves.

title: Carnot: Interpretable, Interactive, and Optimized Execution of Deep Research Queries
blurb: Carnot is an execution engine that compiles natural-language data-lake queries into physical execution graphs and exposes them in an interactive notebook, so analysts can critique the plan, run operators incrementally, inspect intermediate results, or edit the underlying code before a final answer lands. It targets the two failure modes of current AI analytics: deep research agents that hide their reasoning and cost, and semantic operators that get expensive at enterprise scale. The optimizer also lets users set explicit cost or latency constraints on a query.

title: Open-sourcing Metals v2: Databricks’ Java and Scala language server for multi‑million line codebases
blurb: Databricks open-sourced Metals v2, extending the Scala language server with first-class Java support and scaling it to handle its 26M-line Bazel monorepo, and shipped it for Cursor, VS Code, and Neovim. The work let the company pair lightweight editors with coding agents instead of IntelliJ, and by July 2026 92% of weekly active IDE users opened Cursor versus 12% for IntelliJ.

title: Metabase SQLi exploit grants attackers total access
blurb: Metabase disclosed a critical zero-day SQL injection flaw (CVE-2026-72898, CVSS 10) in versions 1.58 and up, giving attackers raw SQL access to the BI tool's database and the credentials, tokens, and API keys for connected warehouses like Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery. Metabase Cloud instances are already patched, but the roughly 2,500 self-hosted deployments Shodan tracks stay exposed until teams upgrade, and OEM-embedded users may not know they are running it.

title: Taking AUTO CDC to the next level: Solving the hardest real-world use cases
blurb: Databricks extended AUTO CDC in Spark Declarative Pipelines to handle bitemporal change data capture, tracking business time and system time as two independent axes so teams can reconstruct both what a fact was and what their systems believed at any past date. Each target table gets four managed columns and rewrites affected history when late or out-of-order corrections arrive, no hand-written MERGE logic required. The capability targets audit regimes like SEC Rule 17a-4, and is landing in open-source Apache Spark 4.2.

title: SafeQL: Search-based Refinement for Safe and Efficient LLM-based Text-to-SQL
blurb: SafeQL reframes the DBMS from a passive error reporter into an active guide for LLM text-to-SQL, repairing only the broken components of a query instead of regenerating the whole thing after each execution failure. Each refinement step is a guided search within a validated "safe query space," converging on an executable query without repeating past mistakes. On the Bird and Spider benchmarks, it beats regeneration-based methods on both execution accuracy and efficiency.

title: AI Query Compilation for Unified and Optimized Execution
blurb: This vision paper proposes compiling hybrid AI queries, both SQL relational operators and LLM inference, into a single unified tensor compute graph rather than shuttling data across execution boundaries. Fusing the two eliminates PCIe data movement between the query engine and the model and opens up global compiler optimizations and automatic sharding. On SemBench Reviews and Movies, the approach hit up to 5.3x lower latency and 9.8x higher throughput on TPUs, though it remains a research roadmap rather than a shipping engine.

title: Looker’s semantic layer governs Gemini Enterprise data for user trust
blurb: Google integrated Looker's governed semantic layer into Gemini Enterprise, letting Looker analysts publish conversational agents natively via the Agent-to-Agent protocol so users query structured metrics and unstructured documents in one chat interface. The semantic layer supplies codified join logic and metric definitions to constrain NL2SQL, giving deterministic answers instead of the inconsistent numbers and hallucinations that raw schema-guessing produces.

title: "Will This Data Break My Task?" - Interactive Synthesis of Task-Aware Data Unit Tests
blurb: This paper introduces PrismaDV, a compound AI system that generates data unit tests by analyzing both the data and the downstream code that consumes it, rather than profiling the data in isolation. It runs LLM-powered steps for data profiling, column-access detection, and data-flow analysis, then maintains a data-code assumption graph linking each generated constraint back to the task's source. The bet is that validation tied to how a column is actually used catches breakage that schema-only checks like Great Expectations miss.

title: A Resource-centric Analysis and Optimization of NoSQL Workloads using Distressed Resource Volume Metric
blurb: Microsoft researchers released open-source NoSQL workload traces from real Cosmos DB clusters, along with a new reliability metric, Distressed Resource Volume, that captures user-experienced quality of service. The paper pairs this with LoadStar, a policy simulation framework, and Orbit, a forecast-driven placement algorithm that rebalances stressed replicas to cut tail errors. Orbit delivered higher load at lower error rates with up to 35% fewer resources, and is already in production with projected savings in the hundreds of millions per year.

title: AkasicDB: Demonstrating Omni RAG with a Unified Vector-Graph-Relational DBMS
blurb: AkasicDB is a research database system that natively executes vector similarity search, graph traversal, and relational filtering in a single framework, targeting RAG workflows that currently rely on out-of-DB pipelines or non-native integrations. The demo runs what the authors call Omni RAG, combining vector, graph, and relational retrieval in one engine to cut the overhead of stitching separate systems together for Graph RAG and filtered vector search.

title: Electric joins Databricks to bring WASM Postgres to AI agent sandboxes
blurb: Databricks acquired Electric, maker of PGlite (a WASM Postgres that runs inside an agent sandbox, browser tab, or device) and a real-time sync engine that reconciles that local state back to a central Lakebase. The deal extends Databricks' Postgres reach from the lakehouse to the edge, giving each agent its own low-latency local database while keeping a governed source of truth in the cloud.

title: Accelerate PostgreSQL migrations using Gemini in Database Migration Service
blurb: Google added AI-assisted code conversion powered by Gemini to Database Migration Service, translating Oracle PL/SQL and SQL Server T-SQL stored procedures, triggers, and functions into PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL inside the Cloud console. The feature targets the "last mile" of migrations, where hundreds of proprietary routines usually demand months of manual dual-dialect rewriting before a move to open-source Postgres or AlloyDB can finish.

title: SiriusDeliver: Automating Data Warehouse Delivery at Tencent
blurb: This paper introduces SiriusDeliver, an LLM-based agent Tencent built to automate production data warehouse task delivery, handling context retrieval, workflow config, code generation, submission, and failure diagnosis end to end. Across a two-month deployment on Tencent Cloud WeData spanning 6 teams and 18,240 sessions, it hit an 87.2% success rate and 73.5% autonomous submission. The A/B test is the headline: median delivery time dropped from 228 to 23 minutes and engineer effort from 95 to 11 minutes.

title: Time to Move on: Querying without Nulls and Bags
blurb: This paper argues that SQL's tolerance of nulls and bags (duplicate-laden, non-normalized relations) is an avoidable mistake, not a necessary evil. Drawing on their work building Rel, a language for end-to-end relational programming, the authors show a query language can run on fully normalized relations with set semantics, dropping both the "billion dollar mistake" of nulls and Codd's corrupted relations. They contend the usual justifications for keeping them collapse under scrutiny, and outline what a null-free, set-based language enables.

title: BigQuery expands data transfers with direct Iceberg ingestion
blurb: BigQuery Data Transfer Service added direct ingestion from GCS, S3, and Azure Blob Storage into Apache Iceberg managed tables in preview, alongside new MCP server, SQL Server, Shopify, and Klaviyo connectors. The Iceberg piece matters most: it lets teams keep object storage as the source of truth for multi-cloud, multi-engine access while still using BigQuery's performance tuning, without hand-built ETL.

title: How to ground Genie Agents in both structured data and documents without losing governance
blurb: Databricks Genie Agents can now ground a single agent in both structured sources (Managed, External, and Foreign Tables, Views, and Metric Views) and unstructured files in Unity Catalog Volumes, replacing the two-system split teams once bridged by hand. Governance lives in the catalog layer: agents run under the end user's identity, so Unity Catalog's object privileges, ABAC, row filters, and column masks filter every answer. The alternative, filtering at the model layer through prompt engineering, makes the LLM your security perimeter.

title: RTA Studio designs mass-timber groundscraper in Auckland as "continuous ribbon"
blurb: RTA Studio completed an 11,500-square-metre mass-timber office in Auckland, using a diagrid structure of locally grown timber to form a curved, low-rise "continuous ribbon" set within a regenerated wetland. The building consolidates offices and research facilities for appliance brands Fisher & Paykel and Haier Australasia into a single campus, part of a broader shift toward timber-diagrid construction for large-footprint workplaces.

title: Pentagram's Marina Willer celebrates music as an art form in new work for De Bijloke
blurb: Pentagram's Marina Willer redesigned the identity of Ghent's Muziekcentrum De Bijloke, a 13th-century former hospital turned concert hall, into a digital-first "living identity" whose swirling, treble-clef-like marks draw on John Cage's oscilloscope experiments. The system pairs that expressive logo with Forma DJR typography and a palette of muted pinks, teals, purples, and blues pulled from the venue's arched ceilings and stone walls.

title: Heatherwick Studio adjusts design of Louisville waterfront park to "restore buzz"
blurb: Heatherwick Studio released updated designs for Belvedere, a park and event space in Louisville, Kentucky, with sections built atop a highway overpass to reconnect Downtown with the Ohio River waterfront. The revision reworks the 1970s-era site to "restore buzz," adding new landscaping and gathering areas across the elevated deck that spans the interstate below.

title: The new 7UP rebrand is bound to be contentious
blurb: 7UP unveiled its biggest identity overhaul in 15 years, pairing a soft retro wordmark and lime-forward palette with a reformulated "Lime Lemon" recipe, just three years after its last rebrand. Keurig Dr Pepper is chasing citrus-leaning Gen Z and Gen Alpha drinkers, but the inverted "lime lemon" naming breaks a conventional word order that will likely draw as much attention as the visuals.

title: Building Tactile UX: Honoring Intentional Design With Lottie
blurb: Isadora Agency's team built Stress Release, a browser-based squeeze toy, without a physics engine, driving every tactile reaction through Lottie's native state API, DOM manipulation, and distance-based math instead of Matter.js or WebGL. The writeup argues that physics engines produce plausible motion while animators produce intentional motion, and that deterministic frame control (down to a 181-frame mega-squeeze) is the right call when hand-crafted keyframes need to survive the interaction layer.

title: Has the world been too harsh on Disney's Hexed?
blurb: A FramebyFrame breakdown on X pushes back against the pile-on over Disney's Hexed, arguing the trailer still demonstrates classic animation principles like opposing directional movement, lead-and-follow, and beat-and-hold timing that keep the action readable. The analysis is a useful reminder that technical animation craft and the reception of a film's design, character, and story are separate judgments that critics often conflate.

title: The CSS hack that extends your website on iOS Safari
blurb: This tutorial shows how to style the areas iOS Safari extends behind the status bar and tab bar by setting a `body` background-color that bleeds past your header and footer, with a CodePen demo. The technique closes the default white gap at the top and bottom of a mobile page, a small polish detail most sites leave unaddressed.

title: The Signal Rail: A Deterministic Motion Grammar for Communicating Conversational Agent State in Terminal Interfaces
blurb: This paper proposes the Signal Rail, a one-row terminal status instrument that gives a conversational agent's motion channel a grammar, mapping states like listening, thinking, and executing to distinct kinetic rules rather than relying on color or a single alive-or-not blink. Its four principles, spatial semantics, one motion rule per state, deterministic golden-frame-testable rendering, and no invented progress, make it a rigorous reference for anyone designing honest loading and status animation.

title: CSS properties you should know for better text designs
blurb: This piece walks through five CSS properties for typographic effects, including `background-clip: text` for masking images and gradients inside live text and the distinction between `vertical-align` (aligning inline elements to a text baseline) and `align-content` (vertically centering text within a block box). It is a practical reference for designers who want poster-style display type on the web without leaving CSS for image editors.

title: What does the sale of ArtStation and Sketchfab mean for digital artists?
blurb: Epic Games sold ArtStation and Sketchfab to KitBash, the company behind KitBash3D and Greyscalegorilla, five years after acquiring both platforms in 2021. The move lets Epic concentrate on Unreal Engine 6 and Fortnite while handing ArtStation's 10 million-user portfolio community to an owner promising to integrate it with production 3D asset libraries, leaving artists to watch how marketplace terms and portfolio hosting shift.

title: GO'C creates multi-use artist building for secluded Washington island
blurb: Seattle architecture studio GO'C wrapped a small stained-cedar building on Orcas Island in Washington's San Juan Islands, built for the Iolair arts foundation as a combined gallery and live-work space for an artist-in-residence. The Eastsound project pairs a public-facing exhibition room with private studio and living quarters, a compact template for institutions housing residencies without splitting them across separate buildings.

title: Cisco pushes urgent patches for actively exploited zero-day flaw crashing firewalls
blurb: Cisco released urgent patches for an actively exploited zero-day in its firewall software that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker crash affected appliances, with no workarounds available. Admins running exposed Cisco firewalls should apply the fix immediately and treat internet-facing appliances as priority targets, since the flaw is being exploited in the wild for denial of service.

title: CISA: Microsoft SharePoint flaw now exploited in ransomware attacks
blurb: CISA added Microsoft SharePoint RCE flaw CVE-2026-45659 (deserialization of untrusted data) to its KEV Catalog as exploited in ransomware attacks, warning that a low-privileged attacker can achieve reliable code execution against unpatched SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. Shadowserver tracks over 8,500 SharePoint servers exposed online with more than 200 unpatched, so teams should apply Microsoft's May updates, enable AMSI integration, and hunt for signs of compromise.

title: Researchers Turn USB Auto-Install Into a Full SYSTEM Takeover on Windows 11
blurb: Researchers demonstrated "Plug And Pwn," a technique that abuses Windows Plug and Play auto-install to reach SYSTEM on a fully updated Windows 11 machine, chaining an emulated Sierra Wireless service and a path-traversal flaw to plant a DLL in System32. An unprivileged user can trigger it locally via an emulated USB device or remotely over RDP when supported PnP and low-level USB redirection are enabled, which Microsoft says is off by default.

title: Researchers Disclose AI-Assisted SharePoint Exploit Chain Reaching Unauthenticated RCE
blurb: Rapid7 disclosed CVE-2026-55040 (CVSS 9.1), a JWT-validation bypass in on-premises SharePoint that lets an unauthenticated attacker impersonate any user, then chained it to CVE-2026-63520 (CVSS 8.1), an unsafe .NET type instantiation in Business Connectivity Services, to reach unauthenticated RCE as the service account. Subscription Edition, 2019, and 2016 are affected; Rapid7 says the July update breaks the chain, so confirm it is installed and apply the pending August package.

title: Hackers Breach Polish Power Plant Controls via Private Cellular Network and Shut Turbine
blurb: Attackers shut down a steam turbine and process-water treatment system at a Polish combined heat and power plant serving 50,000 residents by pivoting from a compromised wind farm to a WAGO controller over the grid operator's private cellular APN, which CERT Polska calls the first observed real-world use of that vector. The controller ran default admin credentials and the APN permitted client-to-client traffic, so defenders should enable APN client isolation, treat the APN as untrusted from the OT side, and rotate default credentials.

title: Zoom Annotation Flaws Could Let a Meeting Participant Hijack Another Attendee's Client
blurb: Three flaws in Zoom's annotation feature let any meeting participant achieve zero-interaction code execution on other attendees' clients, chaining a 128-byte stack buffer overflow with a missing sender-origin check that lets one malformed drawing reach every viewer. Zoom patched the bugs in June and July, roughly two months before public disclosure, with no exploitation reported and none of the three CVEs listed in CISA's KEV catalog.

title: Metabase SQLi exploit grants attackers total access
blurb: Metabase disclosed CVE-2026-72898, a critical (CVSS 10) zero-day SQL injection in its BI platform's /api/session/reset_password endpoint that was exploited in the wild to gain raw SQL access to connected databases, exposing credentials, tokens, and API keys. Metabase Cloud instances are already patched, but self-hosted deployments on versions 1.58 and up, including OEM-embedded ones, remain vulnerable until upgraded and should rotate all connected-database credentials.

title: Full-Key Recovery and Forgery from One MQOM v2.1 Signature
blurb: Researchers published a full-key-recovery attack on MQOM v2.1, a Round-3 candidate in NIST's additional-signature process, that reconstructs the complete signing key from a single accepted signature and forges a fresh message the reference verifier accepts. Full-domain scans for all three security categories cost below NIST's benchmarks (2^142, 2^207, and 2^272 Boolean gates), and salt-bound global-root expansion does not close the one-signature recovery channel.

title: Cisco ASA and FTD Flaw Exploited in the Wild Can Trigger Remote DoS
blurb: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-20349 (CVSS 8.6), an insufficient-error-checking flaw in ASA and FTD software that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker crash the device via a crafted HTTP request to the Remote Access SSL VPN service, and it is already being exploited in the wild. Devices with SSL-VPN, IKEv2 Remote Access VPN client services, or Zero Trust Network Access enabled are affected, so patch to the fixed ASA and FTD hotfix builds immediately.

title: Metabase SQL Zero-Day Attacks Could Have Wide Blast Radius
blurb: A maximum-severity SQL-injection zero-day (CVSS 10, no CVE yet) in Metabase versions 1.58 and above is under active exploitation, letting a remote attacker inject SQL into the application database and gain administrator access to steal stored database credentials, read connected data, and alter instance configuration. Metabase Cloud instances were auto-patched, but self-hosted deployments exposing the /api/session/reset_password endpoint (default API port 3000) remain vulnerable and should be patched and firewalled immediately.

title: Microsoft Patches 398 Flaws Including a Windows Driver Zero-Day Under Active Attack
blurb: Microsoft's August update fixes 398 CVEs, including CVE-2026-68820 (CVSS 7.0), an actively exploited use-after-free in afd.sys that Check Point attributes to Lazarus and lets an attacker with local code execution escalate to SYSTEM. Patch the driver bug first despite its lower score, then queue the four unauthenticated RCEs rated CVSS 9.8 in Windows DNS Server, Deployment Services, QUIC, and HPC Pack.

title: Researchers Built a Fake Crypto Startup and Hired Three Suspected North Korean IT Workers
blurb: Security researchers built a fake DeFi protocol, Ballena Azul, advertised developer jobs, and hired three suspected North Korean IT workers onto recording-enabled work VMs to document the placement pipeline end to end. The onboarding paperwork is the reusable defensive signal: forged IDs with mismatched states, an image carrying a Google SynthID watermark and Gemini metadata, and a stolen license paired with a GPS-stripped iPhone 15 photo. Nobody exploited anything, because each operative cleared an interview, signed a contract, and received authorized access to source code and internal systems.

title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
blurb: Two malicious LiteLLM releases (versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8) sat on PyPI for about 40 minutes on March 24, harvesting cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords before quarantine, and CloudSEK's dataset now maps captured loot to 2,500+ organizations including NVIDIA, Cisco, and FedEx. Treat any install that day through 16:00 UTC as suspect and rotate all CI/CD secrets, publishing tokens, and cloud credentials rather than waiting for proof of misuse.

title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldBreak' zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges
blurb: Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse published "ShieldBreak," a Microsoft Defender zero-day that grants SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server 2025 systems where Defender is enabled. The exploit is a confirmed full bypass of RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656), which Microsoft patched in July, and no fix is yet available, so defenders should treat local privilege escalation on Defender-enabled hosts as unmitigated.

title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code
blurb: SAP patched a maximum-severity flaw in Commerce Cloud's Data Hub Adapter (CVE-2026-58231, CVSS 10.0), where an unauthenticated attacker can abuse a default authentication client to submit crafted input to functions lacking validation, enabling arbitrary code execution. Apply the fixed Commerce Cloud release and re-deploy; as a temporary workaround, configure an IP Filter Set to restrict access to the vulnerable endpoint.

title: Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access
blurb: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8), a directory-traversal flaw in Broadcom VMware vCenter that grants unauthenticated RCE, deploying a malicious cron job with reverse_ssh to establish persistent outbound access, per QUIRSO. Exploitation began August 3, five days after disclosure, and has hit 361 victim IPs across 47 countries, concentrated in Germany, the U.S., and Turkey. Patch immediately and hunt for unexpected reverse_ssh installs and outbound SSH.

title: Lazarus hackers pair fake job offers with Windows zero-day exploit
blurb: The North Korea-linked Lazarus group is exploiting CVE-2026-68820, a Windows AFD.sys local privilege escalation zero-day, in Operation Dream Job attacks that use fake recruiter offers and DLL-sideloaded PDF viewers to reach defense-sector targets, per Check Point. Successful exploitation grants SYSTEM privileges and deploys the FudModule kernel rootkit to disable security monitoring; Microsoft patched the flaw on August 11 in its Patch Tuesday updates.

title: Cisco warns of ASA and FTD VPN flaw exploited to crash devices
blurb: Cisco is warning that CVE-2026-20349 (CVSS 8.6), an unauthenticated denial-of-service flaw in Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software, is being actively exploited to remotely crash devices via crafted HTTP requests to the Remote Access SSL VPN service. There are no workarounds, so operators running affected ASA 9.16 through 9.24 or FTD 7.0 through 10.0 releases with SSL listen sockets enabled should apply Cisco's hot fixes immediately.

title: A Malicious SIM Card Can Run Attacker Code Inside the Modems Behind Cellular IoT Devices
blurb: Researchers at the University of Birmingham and Fuzzware showed that a hostile SIM card can issue RUN AT proactive commands to execute attacker code on the cellular modem inside IoT hardware, and demonstrated full takeover of a commercial EV charger. Nine of 26 tested devices accepted the command, mostly Quectel modules on a Qualcomm baseband; fleet operators should ask suppliers whether RUN AT is enabled in shipped firmware and can be disabled.

title: Malicious SIMs can shut down phones, steal files, and drag 5G back to 2G
blurb: Malicious SIM cards can execute STK-based attacks that force phones to power off, exfiltrate stored files, and downgrade 5G connections to insecure 2G, exposing devices to interception and further exploitation. The technique abuses the SIM Application Toolkit's proactive commands, which handset baseband firmware trusts by default, so defenders should treat untrusted or unattended SIMs as a physical-access threat and restrict swaps in managed fleets.

title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
blurb: Researchers disclosed an architectural flaw in how Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google return encrypted chain-of-thought to clients: the ciphertext blocks are interchangeable across sessions, users, and models, so injecting a stronger model's trace into a weaker sibling forces it to decode the reasoning verbatim without jailbreaking the original.
