blurb: Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed 400 vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock that grants SYSTEM privileges, plus 42 rated Critical. The volume reflects Microsoft's new AI-powered vulnerability discovery system, which it has warned will keep monthly patch counts elevated and raises the testing and deployment burden on enterprise IT teams already managing large Windows fleets.

title: Malicious SIMs can shut down phones, steal files, and drag 5G back to 2G
blurb: Researchers demonstrated that malicious SIM cards can silently shut down handsets, exfiltrate on-device files, and force 5G connections to downgrade to insecure 2G, exploiting the SIM Application Toolkit and over-the-air provisioning channels that carriers control. Enterprises running managed device fleets and cellular IoT deployments now have to treat the SIM itself as an untrusted component, adding supply-chain vetting and baseband monitoring to an attack surface most MDM stacks never covered.

title: OpenAI Pauses Astra Over Cybersecurity Risks
blurb: OpenAI paused its Astra model release after internal evaluations flagged that its offensive cybersecurity capabilities crossed the risk threshold in the company's preparedness framework. The hold signals that frontier labs are now gating shipments on security-misuse potential, which gives enterprise buyers a clearer read on vendor guardrails but adds uncertainty to product roadmaps and integration timelines built around expected model availability.

title: Mozilla revokes Firefox signing key after unencrypted copy lands in GitHub
blurb: Mozilla revoked a Firefox add-on signing key after discovering an unencrypted copy of it had been committed to a public GitHub repository. The exposure forced the organization to reissue signatures across its extension ecosystem, and enterprises that whitelist Firefox add-ons by signature should expect validation churn until the new key propagates through managed deployments.

title: Fresh Windows Zero-Day Exploited in North Korean Cyberattacks
blurb: North Korea's Lazarus Group exploited a Windows zero-day in afd.sys, now tracked as CVE-2026-68820, to gain System privileges in a Dream Job campaign targeting aerospace and defense firms across Europe and India. Microsoft patched the use-after-free flaw in its August 11 Patch Tuesday updates, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, giving federal agencies two weeks to remediate.

title: Coruna, DarkSword iOS Exploits Proliferate Globally
blurb: Sophisticated iPhone exploit chains Coruna and DarkSword, once confined to nation-state and mercenary operators, are now spreading to conventional cybercrime groups, with iVerify tracking roughly 17,000 domains hosting second-generation variants and infections persisting months after public disclosure. Enterprise mobile fleets running iOS 18.4 through 18.7 are now exposed to easily deployed, actively modified attack frameworks, raising the stakes for MDM coverage, patch cadence, and on-device threat detection.

title: Multistate Water System Attacks Widen, Iran Suspected
blurb: Cyberattacks against US water and wastewater systems have spread to at least a dozen states, including Minnesota, Georgia, Michigan, Alabama, and New Jersey, with CISA and the FBI attributing the campaign to Iran-linked actors exploiting internet-exposed PLCs from Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, and Siemens. Attackers are changing PLC passwords and IP addresses to lock out operators, and CISA urges infrastructure owners to pull publicly exposed OT controllers offline immediately.

title: August 2026 Patch Tuesday: Microsoft Fixes 421 CVEs, One Exploited Zero-Day
blurb: Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed 421 CVEs, including CVE-2026-68820, an actively exploited afd.sys use-after-free that lets a local attacker gain SYSTEM privileges without user interaction. IT teams should prioritize the zero-day plus CVE-2026-62832, a publicly disclosed User Profile Service flaw Microsoft expects to be exploited soon, alongside RCE bugs in Windows DNS server and Deployment Services.

title: Cisco Patches Firewall Zero-Day Exploited for DoS Attacks
blurb: Cisco patched CVE-2026-20349, a zero-day in Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker crash appliances into a denial-of-service state via crafted HTTP requests to the Remote Access SSL VPN service. Cisco confirmed active exploitation in August, and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal patch deadline of August 14.

title: Out of band, out of mind: DEF CON research calls IPMI a ‘sanctioned backdoor’ into enterprise networks
blurb: At DEF CON 34, runZero's HD Moore disclosed 123 confirmed vulnerabilities across baseboard management controllers from HPE iLO, Supermicro, Dell iDRAC, and OpenBMC, with internet scans finding roughly 51,000 exposed BMCs and about half handing over crackable password hashes without authentication. Enterprises running these out-of-band management controllers should treat them as an unmonitored attack surface, audit exposure with runZero's new OOBscan tool, and segment BMC ports off routable networks.

title: Nvidia’s $500B AI investment pool could impact enterprise chip pricing, availability
blurb: Nvidia and six finance partners including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, and Goldman Sachs are creating a $500B-plus capital pool to let its customers, from frontier AI labs to enterprises, buy chips on credit at favorable rates. Analysts expect little of the money to reach enterprise buyers directly, and most warn the infusion will push GPU prices higher and deepen the data-center chip shortage rather than ease procurement.

title: ShieldBreak Zero-Day PoC Claims Microsoft Defender Patch Bypass With SYSTEM Access
blurb: A security researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse published a proof-of-concept for ShieldBreak, a full bypass of Microsoft's patch for CVE-2026-50656 (RoguePlanet), a Defender race condition that spawns a SYSTEM-level shell on fully updated Windows 11 25H2 and Windows Server 2025 with a claimed 100% success rate. Microsoft is investigating, but with no fix available and Windows 10 also affected, enterprise Defender deployments have an unpatched local privilege-escalation path.

title: BdThemes Supply Chain Attack Poisons JSON to Create Rogue WordPress Admins
blurb: Attackers compromised WordPress plugin vendor BdThemes by poisoning a static JSON promotional-banner feed, exploiting an XSS flaw in the bundled Biggopti library to inject scripts that create rogue admin accounts whenever a logged-in administrator loads any wp-admin page. WordPress.org has closed seven affected plugins pending review, including Element Pack with 100,000+ active installs, and disabled downloads while the CVSS 5.4 flaw is remediated.

title: Sandworm hackers target IT pros with trojanized WireGuard VPN client
blurb: Sandworm sub-cluster UAC-0145 has been targeting sysadmins and IT staff since May with fake recruiter pitches that culminate in a trojanized WireGuard client, "SopraVPN," which impersonates IT firm Sopra Steria and decrypts embedded PowerShell to plant persistence on Windows and pull follow-on payloads on Linux. CERT-UA advises restricting corporate VPN and resource access to EDR-monitored managed devices, even when staff connect from personal equipment.

title: Kimwolf botnet rebuilt to survive takedowns, researchers say
blurb: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 reported a rebuilt version of the Kimwolf botnet, active since February, that mimics full Chrome browser fingerprints in HTTP/2 floods and resolves its command servers through the Ethereum Name Service instead of seizable DNS domains. The changes let attack traffic blend with legitimate browsing and put command channels beyond registrar or law-enforcement takedown, raising the DDoS mitigation burden for enterprises defending public-facing services.

title: Delta probes Wi-Fi deauth attack on flight carrying DEF CON attendees
blurb: Delta Air Lines is investigating an unauthorized "Delta WiFi Fast" network that appeared on Flight 591 from Las Vegas to Atlanta, which reports attribute to returning DEF CON attendees running a Wi-Fi deauthentication attack that jammed the in-flight network. Crew disabled onboard Wi-Fi for nearly 30 minutes, and Delta says it will work with federal law enforcement and aviation regulators while confirming aircraft safety systems were unaffected.

title: 421 bugs in Microsoft's Patch Tuesday release, and the Norks have already attacked one
blurb: Microsoft's August Patch Tuesday fixed 421 vulnerabilities, one of which North Korean state actors were already exploiting as a zero-day before the patch shipped. IT teams face an unusually large update to test and deploy, and the active exploitation of an unpatched flaw pushes at least that fix to the front of the queue regardless of change-window schedules.

title: SonicWall Patches Critical Vulnerabilities in Discontinued GMS Platform
blurb: SonicWall patched eight vulnerabilities across two products, including two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws (CVE-2026-66147 and CVE-2026-66145, CVSS 9.4 and 9.1) in its Global Management System, the centralized management platform it retired in October 2025. Fixes ship in GMS 9.5.2 and Email Security 10.0.36, forcing IT teams to patch a discontinued product still running in production even though no exploitation has been observed.

title: Mozilla Revokes Firefox and Thunderbird Linux Signing Key After Key Lands in Private Repo
blurb: Mozilla revoked the GPG signing subkey behind Firefox and Thunderbird Linux downloads after an unencrypted copy was accidentally committed to a private company repository, publishing a replacement subkey valid through August 2028. The revocation uses reason code 2, "key material has been compromised," so past signatures on older Firefox and Thunderbird tarballs stop verifying, forcing manual key imports for anyone checking signatures or installing from Mozilla's RPM packages.

title: Feds warn Gunra ransomware is exploiting known bugs to hit critical infrastructure
blurb: US federal agencies warned that the Gunra ransomware gang is chaining known, already-patched vulnerabilities to breach critical-infrastructure operators that haven't applied fixes. The advisory reinforces that unpatched CVEs, not zero-days, remain the primary entry point, putting pressure on IT teams to close exposure windows on internet-facing systems and hold vendors to faster patch-validation timelines.

title: Big Cloud is poised to corner the market for enterprise hardware
blurb: The author argues that hyperscalers' massive AI-infrastructure spending is letting them corner the enterprise hardware supply chain, buying up GPUs, custom silicon, and server capacity at a scale that squeezes out traditional on-prem buyers. The consequence for IT leaders is thinner availability and worse pricing on the hardware they still run in their own data centers, accelerating the shift from owning infrastructure to renting it from AWS, Azure, and Google.

title: Cyberattack on logistics giant CEVA delivers customer data into the wrong hands
blurb: CEVA Logistics disclosed a cyberattack that exposed customer data, adding the freight-forwarding giant to a growing list of supply-chain operators breached this year. Enterprise IT teams that route shipments through CEVA now face third-party exposure risk, since compromised logistics data can seed downstream phishing and business-email-compromise attacks against the customers whose records were taken.

title: PQC in Plaintext: Google Cloud’s post-quantum cryptography roadmap
blurb: Google Cloud published its roadmap to migrate all internal infrastructure and customer-facing services to post-quantum cryptography by 2029, prioritizing store-now-decrypt-later protection, forgery-resistant signatures, and cryptographic agility. The timeline runs well ahead of CNSA 2.0 and NIST IR 8547 deprecation deadlines, and extends PQC into Sovereign Cloud offerings like Google Cloud Dedicated and Google Distributed Cloud for regulated buyers.

title: Delta investigates in-flight Wi-Fi spoofing on post-DEF CON flight from Las Vegas
blurb: Delta is investigating a Monday flight from Las Vegas to Atlanta where a passenger allegedly spoofed the in-flight Wi-Fi with a rogue "Delta WiFi Fast" network to harvest passenger data, prompting the crew to disable Wi-Fi for 30 minutes and authorities to board on arrival. The evil-twin incident, which followed DEF CON, is now under FBI and FAA review.

title: Chrome adopts what may be the best protection yet against account takeovers
blurb: Google added device-bound session credentials (DBSCs) to Chrome on Windows and macOS, binding a browser's session cookies to an encryption key locked inside the device's TPM or secure enclave so stolen cookies are useless on another machine. The measure closes the gap infostealer malware and adversary-in-the-middle attacks exploit to bypass 2FA and passkeys, giving enterprises a hardware-backed defense against the session-hijacking that now drives most account takeovers.

title: Meta can't stop states' $1.4 trillion lawsuit from going to trial
blurb: A federal appeals court dismissed Meta and TikTok's attempt to claim Section 230 immunity from thousands of social media addiction lawsuits, clearing the way for a California-led case seeking more than $1.4 trillion in damages to go to trial on August 19. The 9th Circuit's 3-0 ruling held that Section 230 provides a liability defense rather than immunity from suit, exposing platform operators to consumer-protection trials that could reshape product-safety liability across the industry.

title: Server prices to rise by up to 87% at OVHcloud
blurb: OVHcloud is raising prices on its bare metal and public cloud servers by up to 87%, effective September 1 for new orders and October 1 for renewals, blaming AI-driven demand that has pushed up RAM and storage costs. Enterprise buyers face 59% increases on the latest High Grade AMD Epyc servers plus steep hikes on add-on memory and disks, though existing customers can lock in current pricing for up to four years by prepaying before October 1.

title: Ryanair signs a five-year AI deal with Google Cloud, and a second cloud to fall back on
blurb: Ryanair signed a five-year data and AI partnership with Google Cloud, rolling out Google Workspace and Gemini Enterprise to 35,000 employees and adopting DeepMind's AlphaEvolve and WeatherNext models for fleet operations and maintenance scheduling. The airline framed the arrangement as a dual-cloud strategy, keeping a second provider on standby so critical services survive an outage as it scales toward 300 million passengers a year by 2034.

title: Why AT&T Is Betting Big on Open-Weight AI
blurb: AT&T is standardizing on open-weight models across its stack to cap inference costs and keep proprietary customer and network data inside its own environment rather than routing it to third-party API providers. The bet gives the carrier control over token spend and fine-tuning at scale, and signals to enterprise IT buyers that open weights have crossed into production-grade deployment for regulated, data-sensitive workloads.

title: Zoom flaw let an attacker take over your device, including iPhone and Mac
blurb: Researchers disclosed a now-patched Zoom vulnerability that let an attacker silently execute code on any participant's device during a screen-shared call, affecting Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android with no victim interaction. The notable detail for security teams is speed: firm A Security found the flaw in early June using public AI models and fewer than 20 prompts, work that previously would have taken five researchers roughly six months.

title: Intel raises $19.7 billion to help fund future projects as 14A production looms — share sale attracted $100 billion in demand, report claims
blurb: Intel raised $19.7B through an underwritten public stock offering, selling roughly 210.5M shares at $95 each to fund capacity expansion and next-generation process nodes like 14A, which enters mass production in 2028. The sale drew a reported $100B in demand and gives Intel cash to compete against TSMC and Samsung as it ramps Fab 52 in Arizona and builds its $100B-plus Ohio fab complex.

title: IBM, Together AI team to offer open-source AI inference in the cloud
blurb: IBM signed a $240M deal with neocloud provider Together AI to run a Nvidia HGX B300 cluster on IBM Cloud for large-capacity, open-source model inference. The arrangement gives IBM Cloud an enterprise-grade inference offering to compete with AWS, Azure, and CoreWeave, and positions Together AI's open-model platform, spanning DeepSeek, Nemotron, and Kimi, as a lower-cost alternative to single proprietary models for regulated enterprise workloads.

title: FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers — blockade targets key AI interconnects as China holds 56% global market share
blurb: The FCC is drafting a proposal to add new-model optical transceivers made in China to its Secure Networks Act covered list, which would block their import into the US. The move targets a supply chain where Chinese manufacturers hold roughly 56% of 2026 global capacity, directly hitting hyperscalers that depend on optical interconnects for AI data-center buildouts and forcing them toward pricier domestic and allied alternatives.

title: DEF CON hackers add new muscle to water utility protection
blurb: DEF CON's Franklin project is expanding its volunteer hacker corps to help small US water utilities find and fix vulnerabilities in their operational technology, extending a model that founder Jeff Moss says worked well in the conference's voting village. The program targets the thousands of under-resourced municipal water systems that lack in-house security staff, offering a stopgap as federal cyber support for critical infrastructure stays thin.

title: OVHcloud chief issues customer price warning amid surging hardware costs
blurb: OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba warned customers that prices for some Public Cloud and bare metal products could rise as much as 87%, driven by surging DDR5 RAM and storage costs he attributes to AI demand. The increases hit new orders in September and in-production equipment in October, following similar hikes from Hetzner, Alibaba, Tencent, and AWS, and signaling broader compute-cost inflation across enterprise cloud contracts.

title: Oracle set to bring quantum computing to OCI for hybrid AI
blurb: Oracle will deploy Quantinuum's Helios quantum computer inside a US-based OCI AI data center and offer enterprise access through a planned OCI quantum service for hybrid quantum-AI and HPC workloads, with a preview expected in the coming months. Customers get managed, governed access to quantum hardware under existing OCI identity and security controls, though Forrester notes the integration lowers access barriers without accelerating real adoption timelines.

title: Microsoft reportedly raises Windows 11 license price significantly more than expected
blurb: Microsoft has reportedly raised Windows 11 license prices sharply this year, an increase larger than industry observers anticipated, according to a new report. Enterprise buyers running volume licensing and OEM device fleets face higher per-seat costs at renewal, adding pressure to hardware refresh budgets already stretched by the Windows 10 end-of-support migration.

title: DDoS attacks over 1 Tbps surged fivefold in the second quarter
blurb: Cloudflare mitigated more than 800 network-layer DDoS attacks exceeding 1 Tbps in Q2, a fivefold jump from 130 in Q1 and a 519% quarter-over-quarter increase. The scale, including a record 31.4 Tbps attack from the Aisuru/Kimwolf botnet, raises the bar for enterprises evaluating standalone scrubbing versus infrastructure providers like Cloudflare that absorb attacks inline.

title: Give Palantir up to $244M through 2028, says internal Defense Department memo
blurb: An internal Defense Department memo recommends awarding Palantir a no-bid contract worth up to $244M through 2028, extending its existing data-integration work across the Pentagon. The sole-source justification signals Palantir's deepening lock-in as a government platform vendor, raising the switching costs for federal buyers weighing competitors like Booz Allen or in-house builds.

title: Oracle is putting a Quantinuum quantum computer inside its own data centre
blurb: Oracle and Quantinuum agreed a multi-year deal to install Quantinuum's Helios quantum computer inside a US OCI data centre, sold as a managed service on the same fabric as Oracle's GPU and HPC capacity. The co-located design targets hybrid classical-quantum workloads, but Oracle arrives years behind AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, and IBM, with no pricing, launch customer, or firm date disclosed.

title: Introducing the Developer Device Platform for agentic mobile app development
blurb: Google Cloud launched Developer Device Platform (DDP) in public preview, a fully managed service giving developers on-demand access to real physical devices and high-concurrency virtual emulators for mobile app testing. Positioned as an evolution of Firebase Test Lab built for agentic development, DDP adds a Device Streaming API for interactive remote debugging and a Device Run API for parallel CI/CD tests across hundreds of devices.

title: NIST wants to overhaul its vulnerability database for the AI age
blurb: NIST opened a request for information on overhauling its National Vulnerability Database, arguing that periodic scanning, static prioritization, and manual remediation can't keep pace with AI tools that find and exploit flaws at scale. The RFI asks industry how to build automation, near-real-time enrichment, and auditable AI decisionmaking into vulnerability reporting, signaling that enterprise security teams relying on NVD feeds should expect the workflow to shift toward machine-consumable data.

title: OpenAI targets heavy users with premium ChatGPT Business seats
blurb: OpenAI added a Premium tier to ChatGPT Business at $125 per user monthly, giving select users 5x the usage of Standard seats and removing the five-hour cap, versus $25 for standard licenses. Enterprises can mix and reassign Standard and Premium seats per team, splitting AI budgets into a fixed per-seat procurement line and a variable metered component as vendors converge on hybrid seat-plus-usage pricing.

title: Here are all the new Entra features Microsoft rolled out to IT admins recently
blurb: Microsoft rolled out a batch of new Entra features for IT admins, spanning identity governance, conditional access, and administrative controls that ship without a separate license tier. Several of the more useful changes landed quietly, so admins already standardized on Entra should audit the release notes to confirm which capabilities are on by default versus gated behind policy configuration.

title: Mozilla updates GPG signing key for Firefox releases after exposure
blurb: Mozilla rotated the GPG subkey used to sign Firefox and Thunderbird Linux artifacts after an unencrypted copy was inadvertently committed to a private GitHub repository, though it found no evidence the key was accessed by unauthorized parties. Most users need no action, but IT teams that manually verify GPG signatures or deploy Firefox via RPM on Fedora, RHEL, and SUSE-based systems must import the new key and update packages to keep receiving updates.

title: Daybreak models are now available on AWS
blurb: OpenAI made its Daybreak cybersecurity models available through Amazon Bedrock, adding both Daybreak Blue general-purpose models (including GPT-5.6 Sol) and the purpose-trained Daybreak Red models for vulnerability research and exploit validation. Enterprises enrolled in Daybreak Access can now run these models inside their existing AWS security, governance, and procurement workflows via the Bedrock console or the bedrock-mantle Responses API endpoint.

title: Target taps Lowe’s executive as first chief AI officer
blurb: Target named Chandhu Nair, a Lowe's executive, as its first chief AI officer, tasking him with using AI to improve customer experience across the retailer's operations. The hire signals Target is centralizing AI strategy under a dedicated leader, joining a growing roster of enterprises that have elevated the role to the C-suite rather than folding it under the CIO.

title: Brit rail cops bring live facial recognition to the London Underground
blurb: British Transport Police switched on live facial recognition across parts of the London Underground, scanning passenger faces in real time against watchlists as they pass through stations. The rollout extends a controversial biometric surveillance program already used by the Metropolitan Police, and puts pressure on IT and security teams operating in UK transport hubs to account for how the technology handles data retention, false matches, and compliance with UK GDPR.

title: Together AI embraces the competition with $240M IBM Cloud deal
blurb: Together AI signed a $240M deal with IBM Cloud to fund a large deployment of Nvidia's HGX B300 systems, with capacity launching in Q1 2027. The arrangement pairs a GPU-cloud provider with a hyperscaler it competes against, giving IBM committed AI-infrastructure revenue while Together AI secures Nvidia hardware without carrying the full capital buildout itself.

title: Why observability doesn’t explain what happened
blurb: Observability tools answer what is happening inside a system, but not why. The author argues that root cause usually lives outside the telemetry entirely, in a deploy from two days ago, a spiking support queue, or an approved change record. That gap between seeing and explaining now costs teams two to three hours of investigation per major incident, even when alerting and dashboards are well-tuned.

title: Intel upsizes stock sale to $20B with spending plans still fuzzy
blurb: Intel upsized its stock offering to $20B, but the company has yet to detail how it will spend the proceeds beyond general references to its foundry buildout and balance-sheet repair. The lack of a concrete capital-allocation plan leaves enterprise customers weighing continued Intel roadmap risk as they plan server refreshes and foundry commitments.

title: UK puts £14B cloud framework in place with SMEs promised a bigger slice
blurb: The UK government stood up a £14B cloud purchasing framework covering public-sector buyers, with new procurement rules reserving a larger share of spend for small and medium suppliers. The SME carve-out pressures the hyperscalers and large integrators that dominate government cloud deals, giving IT leaders at smaller vendors a clearer route onto the buying list without displacing incumbents' core contracts.

title: OVH Cloud warns of 87% price hikes to help it cover RAMpocalypse costs
blurb: OVH Cloud warned customers of price increases up to 87% to offset the surging cost of memory, which it attributes to the industry-wide "RAMpocalypse" driving RAM prices sharply higher. Enterprise buyers now face memory-driven cost inflation flowing through to cloud bills, a signal that budget-hosting alternatives to AWS and Azure are no longer insulated from the same hardware pressures squeezing the hyperscalers.

title: LexisNexis pulls three services offline after suspicious server activity
blurb: LexisNexis took three of its services offline after detecting unusual activity on its servers, disrupting access for the legal, research, and risk customers that depend on the platform. Enterprise buyers running LexisNexis into compliance and due-diligence workflows now face an availability gap with no confirmed cause or restoration timeline, a reminder that single-vendor data dependencies carry concentration risk during incident response.

title: Microsoft has joined the growing list of companies cracking down on ‘tokenmaxxing’
blurb: Microsoft imposed limits on staff AI token consumption, defaulting engineers to cheaper models like OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and requiring departments to hit budget targets, per an internal memo reported by 404 Media. The move signals that even AI's biggest backers are treating inference spend as a managed cost line, following Meta and others clamping down on "tokenmaxxing" as per-engineer token bills reach thousands of dollars monthly.

title: Nvidia releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard to give enterprise AI capability options
blurb: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model it claims delivers up to 4x faster output and 30% quicker agentic task completion than peers in its weight class, alongside NeMo Switchyard, an agentic router that directs tasks to the right-sized model. Nvidia is pitching Lightning's cheap customization as the differentiator, citing a partner that post-trained a router agent for $85 in two hours on standard hardware.

title: DEF CON hackers launch Water Watch Center to defend small water utilities
blurb: DEF CON Franklin and the National Rural Water Association launched the Water Watch Center, a program delivering managed detection and response to the small water utilities that make up 91% of the country's 50,000 community water systems and typically have no security staff. Rapid7, Defendify, Legato Security, L1 Secure, and Sentinel Technologies have signed on to share threat intelligence through NRWA after intrusions hit more than 30 Minnesota systems and spread to roughly 12 states.

title: Expanding connectivity in the Americas: Introducing Alisios, Canoa, and OlaLuz subsea cables
blurb: Google announced Americas Connect, a network expansion anchored by three new subsea cable systems, Alisios, Canoa, and OlaLuz, that link the Dominican Republic, Panama, Chile, Bermuda, and Florida, alongside a new Firmina branch into the Caribbean. The buildout adds redundant, geographically separated routes into Google Cloud regions, strengthening capacity and resilience for enterprises running latency-sensitive workloads across Latin America and the US East Coast.

title: Manchester University: from AI initiators to AI integrators
blurb: The University of Manchester is rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot to all 65,000 staff and students, integrating it into Word, Excel, and PowerPoint alongside AI agents like Researcher and Analyst. When the deployment completes at the end of 2026, Manchester will become the first university worldwide to offer Copilot across its entire community, positioning universal access as a way to close the AI skills gap for graduates.

title: IT infrastructure shortages are real and lasting. Here’s how to cope
blurb: Enterprise IT infrastructure lead times have stretched to nine to 18 months and memory-driven prices are up 35% to 200%, as hyperscalers absorb the memory capacity that servers, storage, and network switches depend on. Gartner expects enterprise network equipment pricing to climb over 20% in 2026 with no relief until late 2027, forcing buyers to stretch existing gear and plan purchases far earlier with vendors and finance.

title: Ransomware gangs skip the CEO, head straight for the 40-something IT manager
blurb: Ransomware crews increasingly target mid-level IT managers, not executives, since those admins hold the credentials and access that unlock networks.

title: Microsoft permanently disables OWA Light client in latest Exchange Server update
blurb: Microsoft permanently disabled the OWA Light client in its latest Exchange Server security update, ending support for the stripped-down webmail interface used on older browsers and low-bandwidth connections. The change lands alongside a separate flaw that can still affect hybrid Exchange deployments, so admins running on-premises or mixed environments should test the update before rolling it out.

title: New usability features in Connected Sheets
blurb: Google added two usability features to Connected Sheets: list parameters that let queries reference a grid range of cell values as multiple filter inputs, and column aliasing that swaps unwieldy BigQuery column names for presentation-ready labels without changing the underlying reference. Both let business users self-serve BigQuery analysis through drop-downs and readable labels instead of editing queries, and are rolling out to all Workspace customers and personal accounts.

title: Quantinuum and Oracle partner on quantum compute adoption
blurb: Quantinuum and Oracle signed a multi-year partnership that puts Quantinuum's Helios quantum computer inside Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, letting OCI customers access it directly alongside the platform's HPC and GPU compute. The deal gives Oracle a hybrid quantum-AI story to pitch against AWS Braket and Azure Quantum, and hands Quantinuum enterprise distribution for use cases in materials, drug discovery, logistics, and financial modeling.

title: Improved file importing in Google Sheets with tables and linked pivot tables
blurb: Google Sheets now imports Excel tables as native Sheets tables and fully supports Excel pivot tables backed by table ranges, preserving formatting and linked data on conversion. The change removes the manual reconstruction Workspace users previously faced when migrating Excel files, and it rolls out to all Workspace customers and personal accounts with no admin control, starting August 11 with pivot table support reaching full visibility within 15 days.

title: Nutanix adding AI agent access bridge to its Cloud Platform
blurb: Nutanix added an open-source MCP server to its Cloud Platform, giving AI agents and assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor a governed bridge to run infrastructure operations across hybrid multicloud environments. The server builds on the Prism V4 API Gateway, so connected tools inherit NCP's existing RBAC and access policies rather than requiring a separate control layer, with human-in-the-loop oversight for staged automation.

title: Corporate conversations about AI productivity mostly focus on future gains
blurb: A new report from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis found that most corporate AI-productivity discussions on earnings calls center on expected future gains rather than results already booked. The framing signals that enterprise AI spending remains largely a bet, leaving CIOs to justify current infrastructure and licensing costs against returns that vendors and executives concede are still quarters away.

title: Allstate preps Allie platform to drive agentic AI strategy
blurb: Allstate is preparing an internal AI platform called Allie to anchor its agentic AI strategy, part of CEO Tom Wilson's push to make the insurer technology-driven rather than technology-supported. The build signals Allstate's intent to own its agent orchestration layer in-house rather than lean on a vendor stack, a bet that puts enterprise-wide AI capability at the center of its operating model.

title: Federal vendor with $50M in contracts leaves portal broken for a month
blurb: A ProPublica reporter documents how OPM's FOIA operation collapsed after DOGE cut more than 600 federal information specialists in 2025, leaving requests bouncing between three abandoned inboxes and two broken web portals. OPM's backlog hit over 1,600 requests at fiscal year-end, seven times the prior year, while average processing for a simple request doubled to 84 days. The piece is a case study in what happens when headcount cuts outpace the systems meant to absorb the work.

title: Cisco pushes urgent patches for actively exploited zero-day flaw crashing firewalls
blurb: Cisco issued emergency patches for a zero-day in its firewall software that lets unauthenticated attackers crash devices remotely, with active exploitation already underway and no workarounds available. SREs running Cisco firewalls should treat this as a same-day patch given the DoS blast radius and the lack of any mitigation short of updating the affected appliances.

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report H1 2026: 1 Tbps attacks soar as DNS floods and geopolitical tensions drive a new wave
blurb: Cloudflare mitigated 935 network-layer DDoS attacks exceeding 1 Tbps in the first half of 2026, a 519% quarter-over-quarter jump, as DNS floods climbed to 40% of network-layer activity and CLDAP reflection surged 580% to become the #3 vector. Media and government were the hardest-hit sectors amid coverage of Iran, Ukraine, and the World Cup, with H1 volume averaging roughly 5,300 mitigated attacks per hour.

title: Docker Sandboxes – Disposable, isolated sandboxes for AI agents
blurb: Docker released Docker Sandboxes, a CLI tool that runs coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI inside disposable microVMs with configurable network and filesystem controls, isolating the host from anything an agent does. The microVM boundary makes "YOLO mode" (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) safe to run unattended, and paid Docker AI Governance layers on org-wide network, filesystem, and MCP policies enforced across every developer's machine.

title: A practical guide to solving when zero+zero=two in mesh observability
blurb: This CNCF post explains why distributed traces break when you layer a service mesh (Istio/Kiali) on top of application-level OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and how to reconnect them so mesh and app spans land in the same transaction. The fix hinges on consistent context propagation and an OpenTelemetry Collector that ingests telemetry from both the mesh and the app in different formats. Metrics and logs survive the mismatch, but traces are the piece that silently falls apart until you wire the Collector correctly.

title: A Malicious SIM Card Can Run Attacker Code Inside the Modems Behind Cellular IoT Devices
blurb: Researchers at the University of Birmingham and Fuzzware showed that a malicious SIM can issue a proactive RUN AT command to execute attacker code on the cellular modem, and they used it to take over a commercial EV charger. The flaw hit 9 of 26 tested devices, mostly Quectel machine-to-machine modules in EV chargers, industrial routers, and telematics units, so operators should ask suppliers whether RUN AT is enabled and can be disabled.

title: PQC in Plaintext: Google Cloud’s post-quantum cryptography roadmap
blurb: Google Cloud published its post-quantum cryptography roadmap, committing to full PQC readiness across internal infrastructure and customer-facing services by 2029, ahead of the CNSA 2.0 and NIST IR 8547 deprecation windows of 2030-2035. The strategy prioritizes Store Now, Decrypt Later mitigation, signature integrity, and cryptographic agility, with rollouts extending to Sovereign Cloud offerings like Google Distributed Cloud and to AI workloads.

title: Hackers Breach Polish Power Plant Controls via Private Cellular Network and Shut Turbine
blurb: CERT Polska disclosed that attackers shut down a steam turbine and process-water treatment at a Polish combined heat and power plant by pivoting from a compromised wind farm through a shared private cellular APN, the first real-world use of that vector. The APN allowed client-to-client traffic and the reachable WAGO controller still had default credentials, so CERT's fix is APN client isolation and treating cellular links as untrusted from the OT side.

title: GitHub already has an EDR. You just have to listen to it
blurb: At Black Hat USA 2026, Microsoft's Yossi Weizman and Echo's Mor Weinberger argued that GitHub's own event stream is enough to detect supply-chain attacks that endpoint and network telemetry miss. Studying incidents like Shai-Hulud, Trivy, and Megalodon, they found recurring techniques such as forged commit identities, poisoned tags, workflow abuse, and OIDC theft, with the authenticated pusher rarely matching the forged commit author. Their open-source GitHub Threat Detector ships 22 production and 12 beta rules, correlating weak signals into high-confidence alerts.

title: Why observability doesn’t explain what happened
blurb: The author argues that observability tells you what is happening inside a system but rarely why, leaving teams to burn two to three hours per incident correlating telemetry against deploys, change records, and support tickets that live outside the stack. The fix isn't better dashboards but connecting infrastructure signals to the context that explains them, since support often knows customers are affected before the first alert fires.

title: OpenSSH 10.5/10.5p1
blurb: OpenSSH 10.5 patches an ssh-agent flaw where agent locking broke the session-bind extension, letting operations meant to be local-only run remotely, including adding PKCS#11 tokens and using keys with destination restrictions. The team is now shipping more frequent point releases to get fixes out faster, citing a rise in AI-assisted bug reports, and Portable builds now require ECC support in libcrypto.

title: Advancing AI model interoperability with Docker and ModelPack
blurb: The ModelPack project partnered with Docker to standardize how AI models are packaged and distributed, using OCI artifacts to decouple models from the specific tool or framework that produced them. The collaboration integrates Docker's Model Runner with ModelPack's open format, letting platform teams push, store, and pull models through the same OCI registries they already run for container images.

title: CNCF Announces Graduation of Cloud Native Buildpacks, Advancing the Standard for Container Builds
blurb: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation graduated Cloud Native Buildpacks, its toolkit for building OCI-compliant container images directly from source code by automating language detection, dependency installation, and image layering. The roadmap targets expanded OCI Artifacts support, stronger SBOM workflows, and WebAssembly compatibility, with Bloomberg and Heroku by Salesforce among the active code contributors.

title: Introducing the Developer Device Platform for agentic mobile app development
blurb: Google Cloud released Developer Device Platform (DDP) in public preview, a fully managed service giving developers on-demand access to real physical devices and high-concurrency virtual emulators for mobile app testing. DDP evolves Firebase Test Lab with a Device Streaming API for interactive remote debugging and a Device Run API that fans tests across hundreds of devices in parallel inside CI/CD pipelines.

title: How to Pretty-Print Your Kubernetes YAML as KYAML and Why You'd Want To
blurb: Kubernetes SIG CLI introduced KYAML, a strict subset of standard YAML for writing manifests that parses with existing tooling and no new parser. It fixes the format's known traps by dropping whitespace-sensitive structure, always quoting strings to kill silent type coercion like the Norway Bug, and using explicit braces and brackets. The payoff is safer Helm templating and manifests that mean the same thing to every reader.

title: Accelerate PostgreSQL migrations using Gemini in Database Migration Service
blurb: Google added AI-assisted code conversion powered by Gemini to Database Migration Service, targeting the stored procedures, triggers, and custom functions that stall Oracle and SQL Server migrations to PostgreSQL and AlloyDB. The feature translates proprietary PL/SQL and T-SQL into PL/pgSQL directly in the Cloud console, cutting the months of manual dual-dialect rewriting that make procedural logic the last-mile bottleneck of a migration.

title: Brex watches AI agents at the network layer
blurb: Brex deployed the open-source OpenClaw agent against internal roles, then moved its security perimeter from the code to the network layer after its security team refused to trust an agent with unrestricted code execution. Rather than restricting tool usage the way Nvidia's NemoClaw does, Brex built CrabTrap to monitor what the agent's container actually sends and receives, preserving the coding capabilities while policing egress. CEO Pedro Franceschi argues the coding ability is the point, so the boundary belongs where the code talks to the outside world.

title: Advertisers are trying to influence AI bots with secret ads
blurb: Advertisers are now serving hidden ads to AI crawlers, embedding content designed to poison model outputs and nudge chatbots toward mentioning their brands when users ask for recommendations. As AI search absorbs more top-of-funnel discovery, this LLM-targeted prompt injection points to a new gray-area channel that could distort AI-generated brand mentions and undermine the organic share-of-voice marketers are starting to track.

title: Testing ads in ChatGPT
blurb: OpenAI expanded its ChatGPT Ads pilot to the UK, Mexico, Brazil, Japan, and South Korea, after a US test that showed no drop in trust metrics and low ad-dismissal rates. Ads appear only for logged-in adults on the Free and Go tiers, don't influence answers, and keep conversations private from advertisers, giving marketers a new intent-rich placement inside the assistant itself.

title: Facebook is paying controversial creators to produce rage-bait content
blurb: An ABC News Verify investigation found Meta is directly paying several controversial Australian creators through its Content Monetization program, including a white nationalist with neo-Nazi links and a prominent anti-vaxxer whose pages carry content that violates Facebook's own monetization policies. Meta declined to comment on the specific pages, saying it is "not Meta's role to police offensiveness," which leaves brand-safety and adjacency risk on advertisers whose spend funds the same revenue-share pool.

title: IAB Tech Lab releases new privacy standards
blurb: The IAB Tech Lab released updated privacy standards designed to track evolving state-level laws and standardize how consumer privacy choices are communicated across the ad ecosystem. For marketers, the payoff is cleaner consent signals passed through the programmatic supply chain, reducing the compliance guesswork that has fragmented targeting and measurement as more states enact their own rules.

title: How to make people care about your startup
blurb: Founder-led communication is now one of the lowest-cost, highest-leverage ways to earn attention as AI-generated content floods X and LinkedIn and buries generic startup posts. The piece maps three founder archetypes to distinct origin-story angles, arguing that the goal is not to be vulnerable or contrarian in every post but to say something honest and specific enough to cut through the noise. For founders who reach out saying "I have no idea what to say," the fix is turning your actual origin story into a repeatable comms strategy.

title: Perplexity cites ClickUp 6,474 times. Notion gets 741… Why?
blurb: Roughly half of every AI answer is unsolicited commentary the model adds on its own, and Profound's breakdown shows it clusters in the categories that decide purchases: rationale, comparison tables, rankings, and pricing caveats. Citations and search traffic come from different surfaces, so ranking in Google no longer guarantees you get cited. Notion pulls 5.46M monthly organic visits to ClickUp's 1.77M, yet Perplexity cites ClickUp 6,474 times to Notion's 741. Audit what AI engines say about you, not just whether you appear.

title: LinkedIn playbook offers guide to optimizing for AI
blurb: LinkedIn released a new playbook on optimizing content for AI citations, aimed at helping marketers boost credibility as more professionals query chatbots instead of running traditional searches. The guide covers tactics for earning citations in AI answers, from publishing authoritative posts to structuring content so tools like ChatGPT and Copilot surface it in responses.

title: Study highlights Reddit’s influence on purchase decisions
blurb: A new study found that Reddit users in the US and UK increasingly turn to its communities for product advice, often trusting fellow posters more than family or friends. Marketers should treat Reddit as a high-intent research channel worth active participation and monitoring, since AI Overviews and search engines now surface Reddit threads directly in purchase-stage results.

title: Snapchat ads pharma ad disclaimer links
blurb: Snapchat is adding pharma-specific ad features, supporting multi-CTA attachments and letting health brands surface required safety disclaimers within in-feed display promotions. The move opens Snapchat to regulated pharma and health advertisers who previously couldn't run compliant creative, giving them a younger-skewing channel with the fair-balance disclosure the FDA requires.

title: YouTube announces changes to creator monetization
blurb: YouTube is doubling YouTube Partner Program entry requirements to 8,000 watch hours or 20 million Shorts views, effective February 2027, while existing YPP creators stay eligible under current thresholds. The platform is also adding Shorts ad formats that pay creators 45% of revenue when advertisers target five or fewer channels, part of a push to monetize its 200 billion daily Shorts views.

title: AI search performance KPIs every marketer should track
blurb: Visitors arriving via AI search convert at 4.4x the rate of standard organic traffic, per Semrush, which means a brand can lose 40% of its traffic and still win in AI search while a #1-ranked competitor stays invisible across every AI engine. That gap is why traffic and rankings no longer tell the full story. HubSpot's guide lays out the AI search KPIs that do: visibility, citation share, AI-driven conversions, and revenue impact, plus how to tie each back to pipeline.

title: Google Ad and Analytics add more AI tools
blurb: Google added Gemini-powered insights across Google Ads and Google Analytics, including AI Overviews summarizing traffic and sales shifts, personalized insight cards, a competitive benchmarking tool, and text-prompt dashboards that turn raw data into visualizations. Marketers can now query performance data in conversational language to understand impression-share changes and campaign trends, shortening the path from raw metrics to a strategy adjustment.

title: Meta adds dedicated ad exclusion audiences
blurb: Meta added exclusion-only custom audiences to ad sets, a customer list that can only remove people from targeting and never add them, and can't be converted back to a regular custom audience once created. The use cases are cutting wasted spend on opted-out customers, meeting legal or regulatory targeting obligations, and blocking employees or accidental inclusion as a permanent guardrail.

title: DeadLock Ransomware Uses Polygon Smart Contracts to Make Extortion Infra Harder to Disrupt
blurb: DeadLock ransomware now runs its extortion infrastructure on Polygon smart contracts, storing and delivering victim-communication resources on-chain to resist takedowns, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The group, active since July 2025 and using Session messaging plus Bitcoin or Monero payments, has claimed 96 victims concentrated in Italy, Spain, Poland, Türkiye, and the US.

title: Vitalik Buterin's Ethereum Roadmap Prioritizes Quantum Readiness and Privacy
blurb: Vitalik Buterin overlaid Ethereum's 2023 roadmap onto the Foundation's current strawmap and flagged that privacy, quantum defenses, and a post-EVM execution engine were absent three years ago. The draft plan sets seven upgrades through 2029 and five north stars: sub-second finality, 10,000 TPS on L1 via zkEVMs, 10M TPS across L2s, centuries-long quantum resistance, and shielded transfers on the base chain.

title: Fidelity moves to add staking, quarterly payouts to near $900 million ether ETF
blurb: Fidelity filed to add ether staking and quarterly cash distributions to its $898M Fidelity Ethereum Fund (FETH), retaining 85% of gross staking rewards and passing the remaining 15% to node operators and custodians. The filing follows a November 2025 IRS safe harbor letting grantor trusts stake without losing their tax status, putting Fidelity alongside Grayscale and 21Shares in monetizing idle ETF-held ETH.

title: Bank of England to test stablecoin, digital currency use in cross-border finance
blurb: The Bank of England advanced its digital pound project to Phase 2, working with NOBO Finance, Dun & Bradstreet, and Polygon Labs to test whether public stablecoins and central bank money can settle in a single trade-finance payment flow. The experiments, which use no real customers or funds, target invoice factoring and reusable credit profiles for small exporters awaiting importer settlement.

title: Riot Signs $9.1B, 20-Year AI Data Center Lease at Its Texas Bitcoin Mine
blurb: Riot Platforms leased 191 megawatts at its Rockdale, Texas bitcoin mine to an unnamed frontier AI lab under a 20-year agreement Riot projects will generate roughly $9.1B, or about $457M a year. That is four times the $113.7M its mining business produced in Q2, when Riot posted a $237.2M net loss and a per-bitcoin cost exceeding production value once depreciation was included.

title: Solidity Pro VS Code Extensions Steal Crypto Wallets, API Keys, and Credentials
blurb: Malicious VS Code extensions named "Solidity Pro" posed as Solidity developer tooling while harvesting crypto wallet vaults, seed phrases, SSH keys, and API tokens, exfiltrating the data through a Telegram bot. Yeeth Security found the extensions used delayed activation and heavy obfuscation to evade marketplace review, tracing the campaign to the same playbook as the WhiteCobra cluster that pushed Lumma Stealer in 2025.

title: Coinbase Wins Abu Dhabi License for Tokenized Securities Hub
blurb: Coinbase received a Financial Services Permission from Abu Dhabi Global Market's regulator to build an international tokenization hub, clearing it to arrange deals and custody ahead of a tokenized securities launch. Tokens will be backed 1:1 by underlying shares under FSRA supervision, available only outside the US, with vested holders receiving voting and redemption rights and every transfer subject to sanctions screening.

title: MEMX Files to List Prediction Market-Style Bets on Earnings
blurb: MEMX filed with regulators to list binary contracts on corporate earnings metrics, moving the equities exchange operator into the prediction-market territory dominated by Kalshi and Polymarket. The filing extends a wave of regulated venues building event-contract products, pitting traditional derivatives infrastructure against crypto-native prediction markets for the same speculative order flow.

title: Crypto.com rolls out tokenized stock derivatives as crypto exchanges push into equities
blurb: Crypto.com launched tokenized derivatives tracking 1,500 US stocks and ETFs, including Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla, offering synthetic price exposure to eligible users in the EEA and other approved markets with positions from $1 and round-the-clock trading. Holders don't own the underlying securities or gain voting rights, adding to a tokenized stock market that has grown roughly 600% to $2.49B over the past year.

title: Standard Chartered-backed Anchorpoint begins HKDAP stablecoin rollout
blurb: Anchorpoint, a Standard Chartered subsidiary licensed by the HKMA, began the phase 1 rollout of HKDAP, offering the Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin to institutional distributors and professional investors via beta access. Initial use cases center on cross-border payments and the settlement of tokenized real-world assets, with HashKey Exchange joining as a distribution partner after completing its first HKDAP mint and redemption.

title: The NYC Council sent letters to Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini Titan to investigate alleged deceptive marketing practices and targeting minors (Wall Street Journal)
blurb: The New York City Council sent letters to Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini demanding information about alleged deceptive marketing practices and the targeting of minors. The inquiry adds municipal scrutiny to prediction markets and exchanges already navigating federal oversight, and signals that local regulators are willing to probe consumer-protection questions independent of the CFTC and SEC.

title: Wintermute Plans $1 Billion AI Investment to Compete on Wall Street
blurb: Wintermute plans to invest roughly $1B over five years in high-frequency trading and AI data center infrastructure, pushing the crypto market maker into traditional Wall Street markets. The move follows a slump in digital-asset trading volumes, signaling that top crypto liquidity providers are diversifying revenue into equities and rates rather than waiting for the next market cycle.

title: Russia moves to restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether and USDT
blurb: Russia's central bank will restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether, and USDT on regulated exchanges starting September 1, capping non-qualified investors at 300,000 rubles (approx. $3,600) of purchases per intermediary annually while exempting qualified investors. The per-intermediary structure lets traders exceed that ceiling across multiple brokers, and crypto payments inside Russia remain prohibited under the July legislation these rules build on.

title: Ravencoin, a blockchain built from Bitcoin’s code, could roll back four days of transactions
blurb: Two mining pools controlling most of Ravencoin's hashpower, 2Miners and RavenMiner, are rebuilding the chain from just before the first invalid block on Aug. 7, after attackers exploited a critical flaw to add invalid blocks. The rollback could reverse four days of deposits, withdrawals, and payments, and RVN has dropped sharply as Bitvavo and Upbit halt transactions pending which history the network accepts.

title: Crypto-friendly bank Erebor in talks to raise $1.5 billion at $9.5 billion valuation: FT
blurb: Erebor, the year-old tech-focused bank serving crypto, AI, and defense clients, is in advanced talks to raise about $1.5B at a $9.5B valuation, the Financial Times reported. The round would nearly double the bank's private-market value in months and shore up capital against a mandatory 12% leverage ratio, as deposits climbed from $1.1B in March to $4.6B by July.

title: Two Prediction Markets Shut Down Hours Apart as Kalshi and Polymarket Take 93% of Volume
blurb: Two crypto prediction market startups, Trepa and Fireplace, announced within 90 minutes of each other on Monday that they are winding down, giving users until Sept. 30 to withdraw funds. Kalshi and Polymarket now take 93.3% of the past 30 days' volume across the 40 venues DefiLlama tracks, with Kalshi alone at 75.7%, leaving little room for smaller mechanisms or order-routing layers to survive.

title: Harmony confirms exploit involving unauthorized minting of 4 billion ONE tokens
blurb: Harmony confirmed an exploit in which an attacker minted 4 billion ONE tokens without authorization, corroborating an earlier report from X user Juiceberg. The unauthorized supply expansion dilutes existing holders and threatens ONE's peg, leaving the team to determine whether to fork, freeze, or reissue in response.

title: Coinbase picks Abu Dhabi for its global tokenized asset push
blurb: Coinbase secured a Financial Services Permission from Abu Dhabi Global Market's regulator, establishing an international tokenization hub to arrange investment deals and custody tokenized securities backed by underlying shares. The license gives Coinbase a regulated base to bring traditional securities onchain outside the US, deepening its UAE footprint alongside its Dubai derivatives business and Project Diamond.

title: What’s next for the Clarity Act as September brings a tough road ahead
blurb: Senate Majority Leader John Thune filed for a Sept. 15 cloture vote on the Clarity Act, delaying the crypto market-structure bill's first Senate vote until after the chamber's month-long recess. TD Cowen's Washington Research Group now puts the odds of the bill, which would hand the CFTC broad jurisdiction over crypto assets, becoming law in the next few months at 25%.

title: CFTC flexes emergency authority to keep Kalshi operating amid New York lawsuit
blurb: The CFTC invoked its emergency authority to order Kalshi to keep operating after New York sued the prediction market platform last month, overriding the state's attempt to halt its contracts. The move asserts federal preemption over state gambling regulators and signals the CFTC will shield CFTC-registered prediction markets from state-level enforcement.

title: SEC could propose ‘pivotal’ crypto rules that may start with token safe harbor, TD Cowen says
blurb: The SEC will hold a public meeting Friday to consider proposing a tailored offering regime for crypto investment contracts, which TD Cowen expects could start with a safe harbor for early-stage token sales. The rules would let sponsors raise capital and develop a network without those tokens being deemed securities, then exit SEC oversight once the network no longer relies on the sponsor.

title: eToro agrees to buy TradeZero for up to $231 million as equities drive Q2 growth
blurb: eToro agreed to acquire retail brokerage TradeZero for up to $231 million, expanding its US equities footprint as stock trading drives its business. Net contribution rose 9% year-over-year to $229 million in Q2, led mainly by stronger equities trading rather than crypto.

title: CFTC Sues Goliath Ventures Over Alleged $397M DeFi Liquidity Pool Ponzi
blurb: The CFTC sued Goliath Ventures and CEO Christopher Delgado, alleging the Florida firm raised at least $397M from roughly 1,600 customers to place their bitcoin and ether in DeFi liquidity pools but never deployed any funds, running a Ponzi scheme from November 2022 to February 2026. The complaint says Goliath misappropriated all customer money, paying $87M to earlier customers, $174M to insiders as recruiting commissions, and $48M to Delgado for homes, vehicles, and jewelry.

title: Harmony’s ONE dives 40% after an attack appears to mint tokens equal to quarter of supply
blurb: Harmony's ONE token fell about 40% after an apparent exploit minted roughly 4 billion new tokens, expanding supply by more than 26% against the roughly 15 billion ONE already in circulation. Harmony confirmed the attack, paused its token bridge, asked exchanges to freeze funds tied to four flagged addresses, and is preparing an emergency patch with possible chain rollback options.

title: MoneyGram Brings Cash-To-Crypto Ramps To Solana
blurb: MoneyGram extended its Ramps cash-to-crypto API natively to Solana, letting wallets route users into its retail network without first bridging USDC to Stellar. The integration supports cash deposits in over 25 countries and withdrawals in more than 170, taps MoneyGram's ~500,000 retail locations, and debuts through self-custody trading app Rift on a chain holding $15.73B in stablecoins.

title: CFTC orders Kalshi to continue offering prediction markets in New York after state lawsuit
blurb: The CFTC used its emergency authority to order Kalshi to keep operating prediction markets in New York, overriding a state lawsuit from Attorney General Letitia James that sought to shutter the platform over unlicensed sports betting. The move escalates a jurisdictional fight over whether prediction markets are federally regulated swaps or state-regulated gambling, with billions in event-contract volume hinging on which regulator prevails.

title: Stablecoin Card Issuer Rain Buys Merchant Wallet Startup Ansa
blurb: Rain, a stablecoin card issuer, acquired merchant-wallet startup Ansa, whose white-label APIs let brands run prepaid closed-loop wallets like the Starbucks app. Rain plans to pair Ansa's stored balances with its own Visa and Mastercard issuing so prefunded funds can spend outside the issuing merchant, folding wallets, rewards, and stablecoins onto one platform. Ansa raised $19.4M total before the deal, and founder Sophia Goldberg becomes Rain's head of payments.

title: Brazil's largest lender Itaú is stepping deeper into the tokenization
blurb: Itaú Unibanco, Latin America's largest lender with over $562B in assets, partnered with infrastructure provider OpenAssets to pilot tokenized fixed-income securities and investment funds under an industry test run by Brazilian markets body ANBIMA. The project adds a major bank to Brazil's growing tokenization push, testing how bonds and funds can be issued, traded, and settled on distributed-ledger rails within regulated structures.

title: Robinhood's Head of Product Reveals How Robinhood Chain Hit 200M Transactions in 30 Days
blurb: Robinhood Chain, the company's own blockchain, processed 200M transactions in its first 30 days, according to Robinhood Crypto Head of Product Seong Lee on The Defiant's podcast. Lee detailed permissionless stock tokens that stay redeemable if Robinhood shuts down and an insured DeFi lending product that pays users yield, positioning the chain as Robinhood's tokenized-finance and real-world-asset layer.

title: Australian regulator takes down Yepbit websites as investors report blocked withdrawals
blurb: Australia's ASIC took down Yepbit's websites after investors reported blocked withdrawals, and the regulator publicly denied the platform's false claim that ASIC had frozen customer funds. The action adds Yepbit to a growing list of offshore-styled platforms ASIC has moved against, and leaves affected investors without a clear route to recover deposits.

title: eToro to Buy US Brokerage TradeZero for Up to $231M as Crypto Revenue Shrinks
blurb: eToro agreed to acquire US brokerage TradeZero for up to $231M in cash plus 2.5 million Class A shares, adding a registered US broker-dealer and its short-locator tools to expand equities trading. The deal lands as eToro's crypto revenue fell to $1.35B in Q2 from $1.91B a year earlier, with July crypto trades down 73% year-over-year.

title: Bitwise cuts 14% of staff as crypto layoffs mount during market downturn
blurb: Bitwise Asset Management cut 14% of its staff to roughly 155 employees, joining a wave of 2026 crypto layoffs that includes Coinbase, BitGo, and Polygon Labs. The reduction follows a 31% drop in net assets for its flagship Bitwise 10 Crypto Index Fund through the first seven months of the year, even as the firm continues acquiring staking businesses like Chorus One.

title: Robinhood Chain hits 11.6 million daily transactions as USDe fuels TVL growth
blurb: Robinhood Chain averaged 11.6 million daily transactions last week, a record and roughly 30% above the prior week, while TVL climbed 32% to $473 million. Daily active accounts rose just 3.3% and sit 11% below their July peak, and USDe now makes up ~43% of the chain's stablecoin float, pointing to a fixed user base parking yield-bearing dollars rather than new participants arriving.

title: Florida man charged by CFTC over $397 million crypto Ponzi scheme
blurb: The CFTC charged a Florida man over a $397M crypto Ponzi scheme, alleging he misappropriated $48M of customer funds.

title: ENS Foundation takes administrative control of $65 million Endowment following tokenholder vote
blurb: ENS tokenholders voted about 70% in favor of the "Next Era of ENS DAO" proposal, giving the newly operational ENS Foundation administrative control of the roughly $65 million Endowment and a five-member board to handle off-chain policy, trademarks, and ICANN engagement. The DAO retains its 54.6% token supply and protocol authority but sends a one-time 1 million ENS transfer to fund foundation staff.

title: Twenty One Capital takes $414 million Q2 loss as new CEO plots path to become ‘more than a Bitcoin treasury’
blurb: Twenty One Capital posted a $413.5 million net loss in Q2, with a $401.5 million markdown on its 43,514 BTC holdings driving more than 97% of the total. New CEO Raphael Zagury, who replaced founder Jack Mallers three weeks ago, laid out plans to expand beyond the treasury model into operating businesses, M&A, capital markets, and bitcoin-backed lending.

title: Benchmark sees over 150% upside for Bitdeer on bitcoin mining, AI outlook
blurb: Benchmark reiterated its Buy rating and $22 price target on Bitdeer, implying roughly 153% upside after BTDR shares fell more than 20% Monday to $8.86 on dilution fears tied to a $1 billion shelf registration. The analyst called the selloff an overreaction, arguing Bitdeer's bitcoin mining segment funds operations and made its $4.7 billion, 16-year Volta Tydal AI colocation contract executable.

title: Grvt eyes $100 million USDY position in Ondo Finance tie-up
blurb: Grvt is partnering with Ondo Finance to build a $100 million position in Ondo's yield-bearing USDY over the next year, integrating the tokenized Treasury-backed note into Grvt Earn so its roughly 3.5% yield feeds into users' base rate without them holding the token. The allocation would represent about 4.6% of USDY's $2.14 billion in AUM and return roughly $3.5 million in annualized gross yield when fully deployed.

title: Barça Mobile Plans Stellar Wallet With Wirex and Crossmint
blurb: FC Barcelona's official mobile carrier, Barça Mobile, is building an in-app digital wallet on Stellar, using Crossmint for wallet infrastructure and onboarding and Wirex for payment and card rails. The feature extends the club's existing travel-eSIM app into payments, loyalty rewards, and travel services rather than launching as a standalone product, targeting the carrier's existing user base.

title: Bitcoin's BIP Editors Remove Luke Dashjr Two Days After BIP-110 Fork Stalled
blurb: Bitcoin's BIP editors removed Luke Dashjr from the role on Monday, two days after the BIP-110 soft fork he championed split thousands of nodes onto a chain that has not produced a block since Aug. 8. The five remaining editors cited conflict of interest and inconsistent use of editorial authority, deleting one line from BIP 3 to strip his GitHub permissions.

title: Ether Products Lead $600M Crypto ETP Flow Rebound in July
blurb: Global crypto ETPs pulled in a net $600M in July, their first positive month since April, with ether-native products taking $350M, roughly twice bitcoin's $176M, per 21Shares. The rebound reverses $2.5B and $4.4B of redemptions in May and June, though bitcoin still dominated turnover at 78.5% of July's $133.3B in trading volume.

title: One overlooked group has added $1.78 billion of selling pressure to bitcoin market
blurb: Publicly listed bitcoin miners have sold roughly 28,000 BTC this year, cutting combined holdings from 127,000 to 99,000 BTC and adding $1.78B of selling pressure alongside $4.4B in ETF outflows. With average production costs near $74,300 per coin, squeezed miners are exiting or pivoting to AI, dropping network difficulty about 18% from its November peak.

title: EToro reports second quarter crypto loss even as total profit beats estimates
blurb: EToro swung to a $7.2 million crypto trading loss in Q2 2026, down from a $37.7 million profit a year earlier, as cryptoasset revenue fell 29% to $1.35 billion and July crypto trades dropped 73% year over year. Total net income beat estimates at $0.68 adjusted diluted EPS versus $0.61, but shares fell about 11% as eToro leaned into onchain products and agreed to buy US brokerage TradeZero for up to $231 million.

title: Australian watchdog suspends Cryptolink, forcing 96 ATMs offline
blurb: AUSTRAC suspended crypto ATM operator Cryptolink's registration for three months effective August 9, forcing 96 machines offline after the firm failed to file required transaction reports and ignored an information request. The action follows a June cap of A$5,000 on cash deposits and withdrawals at crypto ATMs, signaling tighter Australian scrutiny of cash-to-crypto services as money-laundering vectors.

title: From Kraken to KuCoin: Entravel raises $7.5M for its push beyond crypto
blurb: Entravel raised $7.5M in a round co-led by Ethereal Ventures and Finality Capital to expand its white-label crypto travel-booking platform beyond exchange partners like Kraken and KuCoin into the broader travel industry. The company powers booking for over 40 crypto and fintech brands, claims access to 2.2 million hotels, and reports booking conversion rates above 10% against an industry benchmark of 1-3%.

title: US Senate advances CLARITY Act ahead of August recess
blurb: The US Senate advanced the CLARITY Act before breaking for August recess, moving the crypto market-structure bill past a key procedural hurdle after months of committee negotiation. The legislation splits oversight of digital assets between the SEC and CFTC, giving the CFTC primary jurisdiction over tokens deemed sufficiently decentralized and setting clearer registration rules for exchanges and issuers.

title: XRP bridge drained for $200,000 after software mistook fake deposits for real ones
blurb: An attacker drained nearly 200,000 XRP (~$200,000) from an XRP Ledger-to-tx bridge that registered fake deposits as real.

title: Bank of England to test stablecoin, digital currency use in cross-border finance
blurb: The Bank of England moved its digital pound project into Phase 2, testing whether public stablecoins and central bank money can operate together in a single trade-finance payment flow, with NOBO Finance, Dun & Bradstreet, and Polygon Labs joining its Digital Pound Lab. The experiments, which use no real customers or money, will inform how the BOE and Treasury let private stablecoins and a potential CBDC interoperate for cross-border settlement.

title: CFTC declares market emergency, orders Kalshi to continue to operate in New York
blurb: The CFTC invoked its emergency authority and ordered KalshiEX to keep operating in New York, overriding the state attorney general's bid to shut down its event-contract markets nationwide. The move escalates a jurisdictional fight over whether prediction markets are federally regulated derivatives or state-controlled gambling, with the CFTC now suing nine states to defend its exclusive authority over CFTC-registered exchanges.

title: Fidelity moves to add staking, quarterly payouts to near $900 million ether ETF
blurb: Fidelity filed to add ether staking and quarterly cash payouts to its $898M Fidelity Ethereum Fund (FETH), keeping 85% of gross staking rewards while 15% goes to node operators like Blockdaemon, Figment, and Galaxy. The move follows a November 2025 IRS safe harbor that lets crypto trusts stake without losing grantor-trust tax status, putting Fidelity alongside Grayscale and 21Shares as staking becomes table stakes for spot ether ETFs.

title: Revolut clinches French banking licence
blurb: Revolut secured a French banking licence from the ACPR and the ECB, adding to its Lithuanian-issued European licence and clearing the way to offer locally tailored products like loans to its 30M Western European customers. The approval follows last year's ECB restrictions over Revolut's product-approval controls and precedes a €1B regional investment and a Paris HQ, with customers migrating to the new licence starting in France.

title: Coinbase Wins Abu Dhabi License for Tokenized Securities Hub
blurb: Coinbase received a Financial Services Permission from Abu Dhabi Global Market's FSRA to build an international tokenization hub, clearing it to arrange and custody tokenized securities backed 1:1 by underlying shares for eligible investors outside the US. Holders will need only a wallet rather than a brokerage or correspondent-banking relationship, though voting and redemption rights are limited to vested holders and every transfer stays subject to sanctions screening with wallet-level freeze capability.

title: Riot Signs $9.1B, 20-Year AI Data Center Lease at Its Texas Bitcoin Mine
blurb: Riot Platforms leased 191 megawatts at its Rockdale, Texas bitcoin mining campus to an unnamed frontier AI lab under a 20-year agreement Riot values at roughly $9.1B, per an Aug. 10 SEC filing. The deal signals miners repricing cheap, grid-connected power for AI compute: Riot projects the lease to average $457M in annual revenue, four times its entire Q2 mining haul as that business ran at a net loss.

title: MEMX Files to List Prediction Market-Style Bets on Earnings
blurb: MEMX filed with the SEC to list binary contracts on corporate earnings metrics, joining the growing set of exchanges moving to compete with prediction-market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. The move pushes event contracts further into regulated exchange territory, testing how the CFTC and SEC divide oversight as earnings-based derivatives blur the line between market data and event wagering.

title: Crypto.com rolls out tokenized stock derivatives as crypto exchanges push into equities
blurb: Crypto.com launched tokenized derivatives tracking 1,500 U.S. stocks and ETFs, including Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla, offering synthetic price exposure without share ownership or voting rights to users in the European Economic Area and other approved markets. The products, issued under a MiFID license from its Foris Capital acquisition, join a tokenized-stock market that has grown roughly 600% to $2.49B in the past year.

title: The NYC Council sent letters to Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini Titan to investigate alleged deceptive marketing practices and targeting minors (Wall Street Journal)
blurb: The New York City Council sent letters to Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini demanding information about alleged deceptive marketing practices and the targeting of minors, according to the Wall Street Journal. The inquiry signals mounting municipal scrutiny of prediction-market and crypto platforms, adding a local-government layer of pressure on top of existing CFTC and SEC oversight of how these venues advertise and onboard users.

title: Standard Chartered-backed Anchorpoint begins HKDAP stablecoin rollout
blurb: Anchorpoint, the Standard Chartered subsidiary licensed by the HKMA, began a phased beta rollout of its Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin HKDAP to institutional distributors and professional investors. The issuer is targeting cross-border payments and the settlement and distribution of tokenized real-world assets first, with HashKey Exchange joining as a distribution partner after completing its first HKDAP mint and redemption.

title: Wintermute Plans $1 Billion AI Investment to Compete on Wall Street
blurb: Wintermute Trading plans to invest roughly $1B over the next five years in high-frequency trading and AI data center infrastructure, pushing the crypto market maker into traditional markets after a slump in digital-asset volumes. The move signals that crypto trading firms increasingly see AI compute and HFT infrastructure as the diversification path onto Wall Street, competing directly with established quant shops rather than staying crypto-native.

title: Crypto-friendly bank Erebor in talks to raise $1.5 billion at $9.5 billion valuation: FT
blurb: Erebor Bank is in advanced talks to raise about $1.5 billion at a $9.5 billion valuation, per the Financial Times, nearly doubling the year-old lender's private-market value since a $4.35 billion round earlier this year. The fresh capital helps Erebor meet a regulator-mandated 12% leverage ratio as deposits jumped from $1.1 billion in March to $4.6 billion in July across crypto, AI, and defense clients.

title: CFTC flexes emergency authority to keep Kalshi operating amid New York lawsuit
blurb: The CFTC invoked its emergency authority to order Kalshi to keep operating after New York state sued the prediction-market platform last month over its event contracts.
